bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第198卷卷第一百九十八

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 198, Volume number one hundred ninety-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 198.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀十四】　起旃蒙大荒落六月，盡著雍涒灘三月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 14] — Beginning in the sixth month of the year Zhanmeng Dahualuo, ending in the third month of the year Zhuyong Zhuotan, altogether a little more than two years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 14] — From the sixth month of 646 through the third month of 649, spanning a little more than two years.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁酉，李世勣攻白巖城西南，上臨其西北。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day dingyou, Li Shiji attacked the southwest of Baiyan City; the Emperor observed from the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the day dingyou, Li Shiji assaulted the southwest of Baiyan City while the Emperor watched from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 城主孫代音潛遣腹心請降，臨城，投刀鉞為信，且曰：「奴願降，城中有不從者。」

translations.literal: The city commandant Sun Daiyin secretly sent a trusted agent to request surrender, coming to the wall and casting down blades and battle-axes as tokens of faith, saying: "This servant wishes to surrender; there are those in the city who will not follow."
translations.idiomatic: City commandant Sun Daiyin secretly sent a confidant to offer surrender, approaching the wall and throwing down swords and halberds as pledges, saying, "I wish to submit, but some in the city refuse."

sentences.zh: 上以唐幟與其使，曰：「必降者，宜建之城上。」

translations.literal: The Emperor gave him a Tang banner and said: "If you truly surrender, you should raise it atop the city wall."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gave the envoy a Tang banner and said, "If you mean to surrender, raise it on the wall."

sentences.zh: 代音建幟，城中人以為唐兵已登城，皆從之。

translations.literal: Daiyin raised the banner; the people in the city thought Tang troops had already scaled the wall, and all followed suit.
translations.idiomatic: Daiyin raised the banner; the townspeople, believing Tang soldiers had already taken the wall, all submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 上之克遼東也，白巖城請降，既而中悔。

translations.literal: When the Emperor had earlier conquered Liaodong, Baiyan City had offered to surrender but then repented midway.
translations.idiomatic: During the earlier conquest of Liaodong, Baiyan City had offered to surrender but later changed its mind.

sentences.zh: 上怒其反覆，令軍中曰：「得城當悉以人、物賞戰士。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry at their vacillation and ordered throughout the army: "When the city is taken, all people and goods shall be given as rewards to the warriors."
translations.idiomatic: Angered by their wavering, the Emperor proclaimed to the army, "When we take the city, all captives and plunder go to the soldiers as reward."

sentences.zh: 李世勣見上將受其降，帥甲士數十人請曰：「士卒所以爭冒矢石、不顧其死者，貪虜獲耳；

translations.literal: Li Shiji, seeing that the Emperor was about to accept their surrender, led several dozen armored men to petition: "The reason soldiers vie to brave arrows and stones and disregard death is that they covet captives and booty;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Emperor intended to accept their surrender, Li Shiji led several dozen armored officers forward and pleaded, "The men risk arrows and death only because they hunger for loot and captives;

sentences.zh: 今城垂拔，奈何更受其降，孤戰士之心！」

translations.literal: now that the city is on the verge of capture, how can we again accept their surrender and leave the warriors' hearts bereft!"
translations.idiomatic: the city is almost ours—how can we accept surrender now and betray the men's hopes!"

sentences.zh: 上下馬謝曰：「將軍言是也。

translations.literal: The Emperor dismounted and apologized, saying: "The general speaks rightly.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dismounted and said, "You are right, General.

sentences.zh: 然縱兵殺人而虜其妻孥，朕所不忍。

translations.literal: Yet to let the troops kill people and seize their wives and children—this I cannot bear.
translations.idiomatic: But I cannot bear to let the army slaughter the people and seize their families.

sentences.zh: 將軍麾下有功者，朕以庫物賞之，庶因將軍贖此一城。」

translations.literal: For those under the general's command who have merit, I shall reward them from the treasury, hoping thereby through the general to redeem this one city."
translations.idiomatic: I will reward your meritorious officers from the imperial stores instead—let that ransom spare this city through you, General."

sentences.zh: 世勣乃退。

translations.literal: Shiji then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji withdrew.

sentences.zh: 得城中男女萬餘口，上臨水設幄受其降，仍賜之食，八十以上賜帛有差。

translations.literal: They took more than ten thousand men and women from the city; the Emperor set up a pavilion by the water to receive their surrender, gave them food, and bestowed silk in graded amounts on those eighty years and above.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand men and women were taken from the city. The Emperor received their surrender in a pavilion by the water, fed them, and gave graded gifts of silk to those aged eighty and above.

sentences.zh: 他城之兵在白巖者悉慰諭，給糧仗，任其所之。

translations.literal: All soldiers from other cities who were at Baiyan were comforted and instructed, given grain and weapons, and allowed to go where they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers from other cities who had been at Baiyan were reassured, supplied with grain and arms, and free to go wherever they chose.

sentences.zh: 先是，遼東城長史為部下所殺，其省事奉其妻子奔白巖。

translations.literal: Earlier, the chief clerk of Liaodong City had been killed by his subordinates; his administrative aide took the clerk's wife and children and fled to Baiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the chief clerk of Liaodong City had been slain by his subordinates; his aide fled to Baiyan with the clerk's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 上憐其有義，賜帛五匹，為長史造靈輿，歸之平壤。

translations.literal: The Emperor pitied his righteousness, gave him five bolts of silk, had a funeral carriage made for the chief clerk, and sent them back to Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his loyalty, the Emperor gave him five bolts of silk, had a funeral bier made for the chief clerk, and sent the family back to Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 以白巖城為巖州，以孫代音為刺史。

translations.literal: Baiyan City was made into Yan Prefecture, and Sun Daiyin was appointed its prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyan City was established as Yan Prefecture, with Sun Daiyin as prefect.

sentences.zh: 契苾何力瘡重，上自為傅藥，推求得刺何力者高突勃，付何力使自殺之。

translations.literal: Qibi Heli's wounds were severe; the Emperor personally applied medicine. By investigation they found Gao Tubo, who had stabbed Heli, and handed him over to Heli to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli was gravely wounded, and the Emperor personally dressed his wounds. Investigators found Gao Tubo, who had stabbed him, and turned the man over to Heli to execute.

sentences.zh: 何力奏稱：「彼為其主冒白刃刺臣，乃忠勇之士也，與之初不相識，非有怨仇。」

translations.literal: Heli memorialized: "He braved naked blades for his lord to stab me—he is a loyal and valiant man. I did not know him at first; there was no private enmity."
translations.idiomatic: Heli reported, "He faced steel for his master to strike me—that is loyalty and courage. We had never met; there was no personal feud."

sentences.zh: 遂捨之。

translations.literal: He then released him.
translations.idiomatic: Heli spared him.

sentences.zh: 初，莫離支遣加屍城七百人戍蓋牟城，李世勣盡虜之，其人請從軍自效。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yeon Gaesomun had sent seven hundred men from Gashi City to garrison Gaimou City; Li Shiji captured them all, and they asked to join the army and prove themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yeon Gaesomun had posted seven hundred men from Gashi City to garrison Gaimou; Li Shiji took them all prisoner, and they volunteered to serve in the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝家皆在加屍，汝為我戰，莫離支必殺汝妻子。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Your families are all in Gashi; if you fight for me, Yeon Gaesomun will surely kill your wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Your families remain in Gashi—if you fight for us, Yeon Gaesomun will kill your wives and children.

sentences.zh: 得一人之力而滅一家，吾不忍也。」

translations.literal: To gain one man's strength and destroy a whole household—this I cannot bear."
translations.idiomatic: I will not destroy a household to gain one man's service."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，皆廩賜遣之。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, all were given grain from the granary and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuxu, they were all provisioned from the stores and sent home.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以蓋牟城為蓋州。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Gaimou City was made into Gai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jihai, Gaimou City was established as Gai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁未，車駕發遼東，丙辰，至安市城，進兵攻之。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, the imperial carriage departed from Liaodong; on the day bingchen it reached Anshi City and advanced to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingwei the Emperor left Liaodong; on bingchen he reached Anshi City and pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，高麗北部耨薩延壽、惠真帥高麗、靺鞨兵十五萬救安市。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi, Gao Yanshou and Hui Zhen, northern nuesa of Goguryeo, led one hundred fifty thousand Goguryeo and Mohe troops to relieve Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingsi, the Goguryeo northern commanders Gao Yanshou and Hui Zhen marched one hundred fifty thousand Goguryeo and Mohe troops to relieve Anshi.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「今為延壽策有三：引兵直前，連安市城為壘，據高山之險，食城中之粟，縱靺鞨掠吾牛馬，攻之不可猝下，欲歸則泥潦為阻，坐困吾軍，上策也；

translations.literal: The Emperor told his attendants: "For Yanshou there are now three plans: advance straight ahead, link with Anshi City as a fortress, hold the heights of the mountains, eat the grain in the city, let the Mohe raid our cattle and horses—the city cannot be taken quickly, and if they wish to return the mud and floods will block them, trapping our army in place—that is the best plan;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told his courtiers, "Yanshou has three options. The best is to press forward, entrench with Anshi City, hold the high ground, live off the city's grain, and let the Mohe harry our herds—so we cannot take the city quickly, and if we try to withdraw the rains will trap us.

sentences.zh: 拔城中之眾，與之宵遁，中策也；

translations.literal: to pull out the people in the city and flee with them by night is the middling plan;
translations.idiomatic: The middling plan is to evacuate the city and slip away by night.

sentences.zh: 不度智能，來與吾戰，下策也。

translations.literal: not gauging ability and intelligence but coming to fight us is the worst plan.
translations.idiomatic: The worst is to misjudge his strength and offer battle.

sentences.zh: 卿曹觀之，彼必出下策，成擒在吾目中矣。」

translations.literal: You all watch—he is sure to choose the worst plan; capturing him is already before my eyes."
translations.idiomatic: Mark my words—he will take the worst course. His capture is already within sight."

sentences.zh: 高麗有對盧，年老習事，謂延壽曰：「秦王內芟群雄，外服戎狄，獨立為帝，此命世之材，今舉海內之眾而來，不可敵也。

translations.literal: Goguryeo had a duilu, old and experienced in affairs, who said to Yanshou: "The Prince of Qin within cut down the contending heroes and without subdued the barbarians, standing alone as emperor—he is a man fated to rule an age. Now he has brought the hosts of the realm; he cannot be opposed.
translations.idiomatic: An elderly Goguryeo adviser versed in statecraft told Yanshou, "The Prince of Qin crushed rivals at home and barbarians abroad to rule alone—he is a once-in-an-age talent. He has brought the empire's full might; we cannot stand against him.

sentences.zh: 為吾計者，莫若頓兵不戰，曠日持久，分遣奇兵斷其運道；

translations.literal: For our plan, nothing is better than halting the army and not fighting, prolonging the days, and sending out detachments to cut their supply routes;
translations.idiomatic: Our best course is to hold back, refuse battle, wear them down, and send raiders to sever their supply lines;

sentences.zh: 糧食既盡，求戰不得，欲歸無路，乃可勝也。」

translations.literal: when grain is exhausted, they cannot obtain battle, and if they wish to return there is no road—only then can we prevail."
translations.idiomatic: when their food runs out, they cannot force a fight, and retreat is cut off—then we can win."

sentences.zh: 延壽不從，引軍直進，去安市城四十里。

translations.literal: Yanshou would not listen and led his army straight forward, forty li from Anshi City.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou refused to listen and marched straight on until he was forty li from Anshi City.

sentences.zh: 上猶恐其低徊不至，命左衛大將軍阿史那社爾將突厥千騎以誘之，兵始交而偽走。

translations.literal: The Emperor still feared they might linger and not come; he ordered Left Guard General Ashina She'er to lead a thousand Turkic horsemen to lure them; as soon as the troops met they feigned flight.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the enemy might hesitate, the Emperor ordered Left Guard General Ashina She'er to lure them with a thousand Turkic horsemen who feigned retreat at first contact.

sentences.zh: 高麗相謂曰：「易與耳！」

translations.literal: The Goguryeo men said to one another: "They are easy to deal with!"
translations.idiomatic: The Goguryeo troops cried, "They will be easy!"

sentences.zh: 競進乘之，至安市城東南八里，依山而陳。

translations.literal: They vied to press forward and pursue, reaching a point eight li southeast of Anshi City, where they formed battle lines along the hills.
translations.idiomatic: They charged in pursuit to a point eight li southeast of Anshi City and formed their line along the hills.

sentences.zh: 上悉召諸將問計，長孫無忌對曰：「臣聞臨敵將戰，必先觀士卒之情。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned all the generals to ask their plans; Zhangsun Wuji replied: "Your servant has heard that on the eve of battle one must first observe the soldiers' mood.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor called his generals for counsel. Zhangsun Wuji answered, "Before battle one must read the troops' spirit.

sentences.zh: 臣適行經諸營，見士卒聞高麗至，皆拔刀結旆，喜形於色，此必勝之兵也。

translations.literal: Your servant has just passed through the camps and saw that when the soldiers heard the Goguryeo had come, they all drew blades and tied banners, joy plain on their faces—this is an army that will surely win.
translations.idiomatic: I have just toured the camps. When the men heard the Goguryeo were coming, they drew swords and fixed their banners with joy on their faces—this is an army that will win.

sentences.zh: 陛下未冠，身親行陳，凡出奇制勝，皆上稟聖謀，諸將奉成算而已。

translations.literal: Before Your Majesty had come of age you personally took the field; every stroke of surprise and victory has rested on the sage plans from above, and the generals merely carry out the completed calculations.
translations.idiomatic: Since before you came of age you have led armies yourself; every brilliant victory has been your design, and we generals only execute your plans.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，乞陛下指蹤。」

translations.literal: In today's affair, I beg Your Majesty to point the way."
translations.idiomatic: For today's battle, I beg Your Majesty to direct us."

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「諸公以此見讓，朕當為諸公商度。」

translations.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "You gentlemen yield the honor to me in this way; I shall deliberate for you all."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor smiled and said, "You defer to me—then I shall plan this battle for you."

sentences.zh: 乃與無忌等從數百騎乘高望之，觀山川形勢，可以伏兵及出入之所。

translations.literal: He then went with Wuji and others, several hundred horsemen following, to ride up high and survey the terrain—where ambushes might lie and where troops could enter or exit.
translations.idiomatic: He then rode to high ground with Wuji and several hundred horsemen to study the terrain for ambush sites and avenues of attack.

sentences.zh: 高麗、靺鞨合兵為陳，長四十里。

translations.literal: The Goguryeo and Mohe combined their forces into a battle array forty li long.
translations.idiomatic: The combined Goguryeo and Mohe army formed a battle line forty li long.

sentences.zh: 江夏王道宗曰：「高麗傾國以拒王師，平壤之守必弱，願假臣精卒五千，覆其本根，則數十萬之眾可不戰而降。」

translations.literal: Prince of Jiangxia Li Daozong said: "Goguryeo has staked the nation to resist the royal army; the defense of Pyongyang must be weak. I beg five thousand picked troops to strike their root, and then these hundreds of thousands can be made to surrender without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong said, "Goguryeo has thrown everything against us—Pyongyang must be thinly defended. Give me five thousand elite troops to strike their capital, and this army of hundreds of thousands will collapse without a fight."

sentences.zh: 上不應，遣使紿延壽曰：「我以爾國強臣弒其主，故來問罪；

translations.literal: The Emperor did not reply and sent an envoy to deceive Yanshou, saying: "I have come to demand punishment because a powerful minister in your state murdered his sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not answer but sent an envoy to deceive Yanshou, saying, "I came because your powerful ministers murdered their king;

sentences.zh: 至於交戰，非吾本心。

translations.literal: as for giving battle, that is not my true intent.
translations.idiomatic: fighting was never my wish.

sentences.zh: 入爾境，芻粟不給，故取爾數城，俟爾國修臣禮，則所失必復矣。」

translations.literal: Entering your territory, fodder and grain were not supplied, so I took several of your cities; when your state restores the rites of a subject, what was lost will surely be returned."
translations.idiomatic: Your land gave us no fodder, so I seized a few cities. Restore your vassal duties and you will have them back."

sentences.zh: 延壽信之，不復設備。

translations.literal: Yanshou believed it and made no further preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou believed him and let his guard down.

sentences.zh: 上夜召文武計事，命李世勣將步騎萬五千陳於西嶺；

translations.literal: That night the Emperor summoned civil and military officials to plan and ordered Li Shiji to lead fifteen thousand infantry and cavalry to form battle lines on the western ridge;
translations.idiomatic: That night the Emperor convened his officials and ordered Li Shiji to deploy fifteen thousand infantry and cavalry on the western ridge;

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌將精兵萬一千為奇兵，自山北出於狹谷以沖其後。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji was to lead eleven thousand picked troops as a surprise force, coming out from a narrow valley north of the mountains to strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji would lead eleven thousand elite troops as a flanking force through a northern gorge to strike the enemy rear.

sentences.zh: 上自將步騎四千，挾鼓角，偃旗幟，登北山上，敕諸軍聞鼓角齊出奮擊。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself led four thousand infantry and cavalry with drums and horns, banners lowered, and climbed the northern hill, ordering all armies at the sound of drum and horn to charge out together in fierce attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally took four thousand troops with drums and horns concealed, banners furled, onto the northern hill and ordered every unit to charge when the signal sounded.

sentences.zh: 因命有司張受降幕於朝堂之側。

translations.literal: He also ordered the officials to pitch a surrender-receiving tent beside the command pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered a surrender tent erected beside headquarters.

sentences.zh: 戊午，延壽等獨見李世勣布陳，勒兵欲戰。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Yanshou and the others saw only Li Shiji deploying his array and marshaled their troops to fight.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuwu, Yanshou saw only Li Shiji's formation deployed and drew up his men for battle.

sentences.zh: 上望見無忌軍塵起，命作鼓角，舉旗幟，諸軍鼓噪並進，延壽等大懼，欲分兵御之，而其陳已亂。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw the dust of Wuji's army rise, ordered drums and horns sounded and banners raised; all armies shouted and advanced together. Yanshou and the others were greatly afraid and wished to divide troops to meet them, but their array was already in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wuji's dust cloud rise, the Emperor sounded drums and horns and raised his banners. The whole army roared forward. Yanshou tried to divide his forces to respond, but his line was already breaking.

sentences.zh: 會有雷電，龍門人薛仁貴著奇服，大呼陷陳，所向無敵；

translations.literal: Just then there was thunder and lightning; Xue Rengui of Longmen, wearing striking garb, shouted and broke into the array, nowhere meeting resistance;
translations.idiomatic: Thunder cracked as Xue Rengui of Longmen, in dazzling armor, charged the enemy line shouting—and cut down all before him;

sentences.zh: 高麗兵披靡，大軍乘之，高麗兵大潰，斬首二萬餘級。

translations.literal: the Goguryeo troops were routed; the great army pressed them and the Goguryeo army fled in utter collapse, with more than twenty thousand heads cut off.
translations.idiomatic: the Goguryeo ranks crumbled; the main army swept in and routed them, taking more than twenty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 上望見仁貴，召見，拜游擊將軍。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw Rengui, summoned him, and appointed him General of Mobile Attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor spotted Rengui, summoned him, and made him a general of mobile attack.

sentences.zh: 仁貴，安都之六世孫，名禮，以字行。

translations.literal: Rengui was the sixth-generation descendant of Andu; his given name was Li and he was known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui was a sixth-generation descendant of Andu; his personal name was Li, but he went by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 延壽等將餘眾依山自固，上命諸軍圍之，長孫無忌悉撤橋樑，斷其歸路。

translations.literal: Yanshou and the others led the remaining troops to hold fast along the hills; the Emperor ordered all armies to surround them, and Zhangsun Wuji removed every bridge, cutting off their route of return.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou rallied the survivors on the hills. The Emperor ordered a full encirclement, and Zhangsun Wuji tore down every bridge to cut off retreat.

sentences.zh: 己未，延壽、惠真帥其眾三萬六千八百人請降，入軍門，膝行而前，拜伏請命。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Yanshou and Hui Zhen led their thirty-six thousand eight hundred men to request surrender; they entered the camp gate, advanced on their knees, and bowed prostrate to beg for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei, Yanshou and Hui Zhen surrendered with thirty-six thousand eight hundred men, crawling on their knees through the camp gate to beg mercy.

sentences.zh: 上語之曰：「東夷少年，跳梁海曲，至於摧堅決勝，故當不及老人，自今復敢與天子戰乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor addressed them: "You young men of the eastern barbarians capered along the coast; as for breaking strong points and deciding victory, that surely cannot match an old man. From today on, do you dare fight the Son of Heaven again?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told them, "You eastern youths strutted along the shore—but when it came to breaking a hardened foe and winning the day, you were no match for an old man. Will you dare fight the Son of Heaven again?"

sentences.zh: 皆伏地不能對。

translations.literal: They all lay prostrate and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: They lay facedown and could not reply.

sentences.zh: 上簡耨薩已下酋長三千五百人，授以戎秩，遷之內地，餘皆縱之，使還平壤；

translations.literal: The Emperor selected thirty-five hundred chieftains from the rank of nuesa downward, gave them military ranks, and moved them inland; the rest were all released and sent back to Pyongyang;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor chose thirty-five hundred chieftains of nuesa rank and below, gave them military titles, and resettled them inland; the rest he released to return to Pyongyang;

sentences.zh: 皆雙舉手以顙頓地，歡呼聞數十里外。

translations.literal: they all raised both hands and knocked their foreheads on the ground; their shouts of joy were heard tens of li away.
translations.idiomatic: they raised both hands and kowtowed, their cheers audible for tens of li.

sentences.zh: 收靺鞨三千三百人，悉坑之。

translations.literal: Three thousand three hundred Mohe were taken and all were buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand three hundred Mohe prisoners were taken and all buried alive.

sentences.zh: 獲馬五萬匹，牛五萬頭，鐵甲萬領，他器械稱是。

translations.literal: They captured fifty thousand horses, fifty thousand cattle, ten thousand suits of iron armor, and other weapons in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: The spoils included fifty thousand horses, fifty thousand cattle, ten thousand suits of iron armor, and comparable quantities of other arms.

sentences.zh: 高麗舉國大駭，後黃城、銀城皆自拔遁去，數百里無復人煙。

translations.literal: All Goguryeo was greatly terrified; Houhuang City and Yincheng both abandoned themselves and fled, and for several hundred li there was again no human habitation.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo was shaken to its core; Houhuang and Yincheng were abandoned, and for hundreds of li the land lay empty.

sentences.zh: 上驛書報太子，仍與高士廉等書曰：「朕為將如此，何如？」

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a dispatch by post to report to the Crown Prince, and also wrote to Gao Shilian and others: "As a general I am like this—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a courier dispatch to the Crown Prince and wrote to Gao Shilian and others, "As a commander, how do you rate me?"

sentences.zh: 更名所幸山曰駐驆山。

translations.literal: He renamed the hill where he had halted his carriage Mount Zhuma.
translations.idiomatic: He renamed the hill where he had camped Mount Halting-the-Carriage.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛未，上徙營安市城東嶺。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day xinwei, the Emperor moved camp to the eastern ridge of Anshi City.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the day xinwei, the Emperor shifted camp to the eastern ridge above Anshi City.

sentences.zh: 己卯，詔標識戰死者屍，俟軍還與之俱歸。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, an edict ordered the bodies of the war dead to be marked, to be brought home together when the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao, he ordered the fallen marked so their bodies could be brought home with the army.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以高延壽為鴻臚卿，高惠真為司農卿。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, Gao Yanshou was made Minister of Ceremonial Reception and Gao Hui Zhen was made Minister of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wuzi, Gao Yanshou was appointed Minister of Ceremonial Reception and Gao Hui Zhen Minister of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 張亮軍過建安城下，壁壘未固，士卒多出樵牧，高麗兵奄至，軍中駭擾。

translations.literal: Zhang Liang's army passed below Jian'an City; the ramparts were not yet secure and many soldiers had gone out to gather firewood and pasture animals when Goguryeo troops suddenly arrived and the army was thrown into alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liang's column passed Jian'an City before its defenses were finished. Many men were out foraging when Goguryeo troops struck suddenly and panic spread through the camp.

sentences.zh: 亮素怯，踞胡床，直視不言，將士見之，更以為勇。

translations.literal: Liang was by nature timid; he sat on a barbarian camp-stool, stared straight ahead, and said nothing—the officers and men, seeing this, took it all the more for courage.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was a coward by nature, but he sat on his camp stool staring ahead in silence—and the men took his stillness for bravery.

sentences.zh: 總管張金樹等鳴鼓勒兵擊高麗，破之。

translations.literal: Commandant Zhang Jinshu and others sounded drums, marshaled the troops, attacked the Goguryeo, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Zhang Jinshu and others beat the drums, rallied the men, attacked, and routed the Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲辰，候騎獲莫離支諜者高竹離，反接詣軍門。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day jiachen, scout horsemen captured Yeon Gaesomun's spy Gao Zhuli, bound him with arms reversed, and brought him to the camp gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the day jiachen, scouts seized Yeon Gaesomun's spy Gao Zhuli with his arms bound behind him and brought him to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 上召見，解縛問曰：「何瘦之甚？」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned and saw him, untied his bonds, and asked: "Why are you so thin?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received him, cut his bonds, and asked, "Why are you so thin?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「竅道間行，不食數日矣。」

translations.literal: He answered: "I traveled by hidden paths and have not eaten for several days."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I came by secret paths and have not eaten for days."

sentences.zh: 命賜之食，謂曰：「爾為諜，宜速反命。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered food given him and said: "You are a spy—you should hurry back with your report.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor fed him and said, "You are a spy—go report back at once.

sentences.zh: 為我寄語莫離支：欲知軍中消息，可遣人徑詣吾所，何必間行辛苦也！」

translations.literal: Convey to Yeon Gaesomun for me: if he wishes to know news of the army, he may send someone straight to my headquarters—why must he travel by secret paths in such hardship!"
translations.idiomatic: Tell Yeon Gaesomun: if he wants news of my army, he may send envoys directly to me—why torture himself with secret routes?"

sentences.zh: 竹離徒跣，上賜屩而遣之。

translations.literal: Zhuli was barefoot; the Emperor gave him sandals and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuli was barefoot; the Emperor gave him shoes and sent him on his way.

sentences.zh: 丙午，徙營於安市城南。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, the camp was moved south of Anshi City.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu, the army moved camp south of Anshi City.

sentences.zh: 上在遼外，凡置營，但明斥候，不為塹壘，雖逼其城，高麗終不敢出為寇抄，軍士單行野宿如中國焉。

translations.literal: While the Emperor was beyond Liaodong, whenever he set camp he only posted clear scouts and did not dig trenches or ramparts; though pressing close to their cities, Goguryeo in the end did not dare come out to raid, and soldiers traveled alone and slept in the open as if in China itself.
translations.idiomatic: In Liaodong the Emperor camped with strong scouting but no trenches or walls. Even pressed against enemy cities, Goguryeo never dared raid, and his men walked and slept in the open as safely as at home.

sentences.zh: 上之將伐高麗也，薛延陀遣使入貢，上謂之曰：「語爾可汗：今我父子東征高麗，汝能為寇，宜亟來！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to attack Goguryeo, the Xueyantuo sent envoys with tribute; the Emperor told them: "Tell your qaghan: now my father and son are campaigning east against Goguryeo—if you can raid us, you had best come quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: Before the Goguryeo campaign, Xueyantuo sent tribute envoys. The Emperor told them, "Tell your qaghan: my son and I are marching east against Goguryeo—if he means to raid us, let him come at once!"

sentences.zh: 真珠可汗惶恐，遣使致謝，且請發兵助軍；

translations.literal: Qaghan Zhenzhu was fearful and sent envoys to apologize and also to request permission to send troops to aid the army;
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Zhenzhu was terrified and sent envoys to apologize and offer troops to assist the campaign;

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 及高麗敗於駐驆山，莫離支使靺鞨說真珠，啖以厚利，真珠懾服不敢動。

translations.literal: When Goguryeo was defeated at Mount Zhuma, Yeon Gaesomun sent Mohe to persuade Zhenzhu, tempting him with rich profit; Zhenzhu was cowed and did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: After Goguryeo's defeat at Mount Halting-the-Carriage, Yeon Gaesomun sent Mohe to woo Zhenzhu with rich bribes, and the qaghan, intimidated, held still.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬申，真珠卒，上為之發哀。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day renshen, Zhenzhu died; the Emperor mourned for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the day renshen, Zhenzhu died, and the Emperor observed mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 初，真珠請以其庶長子曳莽為突利失可汗，居東方，統雜種；

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhenzhu had requested that his eldest son by a concubine, Yemang, be made Qaghan Tuli Shi, dwelling in the east and ruling the mixed tribes;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhenzhu had asked that his eldest son by a concubine, Yemang, be made Qaghan Tuli Shi in the east to rule the mixed tribes;

sentences.zh: 嫡子拔灼為肆葉護可汗，居西方，統薛延陀；

translations.literal: his legitimate son Bazhuo was to be Qaghan Siye Hu, dwelling in the west and ruling the Xueyantuo;
translations.idiomatic: his legitimate son Bazhuo was to be Qaghan Siye Hu in the west to rule the Xueyantuo core;

sentences.zh: 詔許之，皆以禮冊命。

translations.literal: an edict approved this, and both were invested with ritual patent.
translations.idiomatic: the court approved and invested both by formal ceremony.

sentences.zh: 曳莽性躁擾，輕用兵，與拔灼不協。

translations.literal: Yemang was by nature restless and rash, lightly resorting to arms, and was not on good terms with Bazhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yemang was impulsive and quick to fight and did not get along with Bazhuo.

sentences.zh: 真珠卒，來會喪。

translations.literal: When Zhenzhu died, they came to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzhu died, both came for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 既葬，曳莽恐拔灼圖己，先還所部，拔灼追襲殺之，自立為頡利俱利薛沙多彌可汗。

translations.literal: After the burial, Yemang feared Bazhuo would plot against him and returned first to his territory; Bazhuo pursued, attacked, and killed him, then installed himself as Qaghan Jieli Julixue Shaduomi.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial, fearing Bazhuo would move against him, Yemang hurried back to his domain; Bazhuo overtook and killed him and proclaimed himself Qaghan Jieli Julixue Shaduomi.

sentences.zh: 上之克白巖也，謂李世勣曰：「吾聞安市城險而兵精，其城主材勇，莫離支之亂，城守不服，莫離支擊之不能下，因而與之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor had taken Baiyan, he said to Li Shiji: "I have heard that Anshi City is perilous and its troops elite, that its commandant is talented and brave; during Yeon Gaesomun's rebellion the city garrison would not submit, Gaesomun could not take it by attack, and therefore gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Baiyan, the Emperor told Li Shiji, "I hear Anshi is strong and well garrisoned, and its commandant gifted and bold. In Yeon Gaesomun's revolt the city refused to submit; Gaesomun could not take it and therefore granted it to him.

sentences.zh: 建安兵弱而糧少，若出其不意，攻之必克。

translations.literal: Jian'an has weak troops and little grain; if we strike by surprise, the attack is sure to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an is weakly garrisoned and short of food—a surprise attack would surely take it.

sentences.zh: 公可先攻建安，建安下，則安市在吾腹中，此兵法所謂『城有所不攻』者也。」

translations.literal: Your Grace may first attack Jian'an; when Jian'an falls, Anshi will be in our belly—this is what the art of war calls 'there are cities one does not attack.'"
translations.idiomatic: Attack Jian'an first. Once it falls, Anshi is ours for the taking—that is the art of war's 'cities you do not assault' in reverse."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「建安在南，安市在北，吾軍糧皆在遼東；

translations.literal: He replied: "Jian'an is in the south and Anshi in the north; all our army's grain is in Liaodong;
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Jian'an lies south and Anshi north, and all our supplies are in Liaodong;

sentences.zh: 今逾安市而攻建安，若賊斷吾運道，將若之何？

translations.literal: if we now pass beyond Anshi to attack Jian'an and the enemy cuts our supply route, what then?
translations.idiomatic: if we bypass Anshi for Jian'an and the enemy severs our supply line, what then?

sentences.zh: 不如先攻安市，安市下，則鼓行而取建安耳。」

translations.literal: It is better to attack Anshi first; when Anshi falls, we can march with drums beating and take Jian'an."
translations.idiomatic: Better to take Anshi first, then march in triumph on Jian'an."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「以公為將，安得不用公策。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "With you as general, how could I not use your plan?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You are my general—of course I follow your plan.

sentences.zh: 勿誤吾事！」

translations.literal: Do not ruin my affair!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not botch this for me!"

sentences.zh: 世勣遂攻安市。

translations.literal: Shiji then attacked Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji thereupon besieged Anshi.

sentences.zh: 安市人望見上旗蓋，輒乘城鼓噪，上怒，世勣請克城之日，男子皆坑之。

translations.literal: Whenever the people of Anshi saw the Emperor's banner and canopy they would mount the wall and shout; the Emperor was angry, and Shiji requested that on the day the city was taken all the men be buried alive.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the people of Anshi saw the imperial banner they jeered from the walls. Enraged, the Emperor agreed when Shiji asked that every man in the city be put to death on the day it fell.

sentences.zh: 安市人聞之，益堅守，攻久不下。

translations.literal: When the people of Anshi heard this, they defended all the more stubbornly, and the attack could not succeed for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the defenders fought all the harder, and the siege dragged on.

sentences.zh: 高延壽、高惠真請於上曰：「奴既委身大國，不敢不獻其誠，欲天子早成大功，奴得與妻子相見。

translations.literal: Gao Yanshou and Gao Hui Zhen petitioned the Emperor: "Your slaves having entrusted themselves to the great state, we dare not withhold our sincerity; we wish the Son of Heaven to achieve great success early so that we may see our wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanshou and Gao Hui Zhen pleaded, "We have submitted to the empire and owe you our utmost loyalty. Grant the Son of Heaven swift victory so we may see our families again.

sentences.zh: 安市人顧惜其家，人自為戰，未易猝拔。

translations.literal: The people of Anshi cherish their families and each fights for himself; the city cannot easily be taken in a rush.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Anshi fight for their homes, each man for himself—the city will not fall quickly.

sentences.zh: 今奴以高麗十餘萬眾，望旗沮潰，國人膽破，烏骨城耨薩老耄，不能堅守，移兵臨之，朝至夕克。

translations.literal: Now your slaves, with more than a hundred thousand Goguryeo troops, saw the banners and their courage collapsed; the nation's heart is broken. The nuesa of Wugu City is old and feeble and cannot hold firm—move the army against it and it will fall from morning to evening.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand of us collapsed at your banners—the kingdom is terrified. Wugu's garrison commander is old and weak. March on him and the city will fall in a day.

sentences.zh: 其餘當道小城，必望風奔潰。

translations.literal: The other small cities along the route will surely flee at the sight of your banners.
translations.idiomatic: Every other town on the road will scatter before you.

sentences.zh: 然後收其資糧，鼓行而前，平壤必不守矣。」

translations.literal: Then gather their grain and supplies, advance with drums beating, and Pyongyang will surely not be held."
translations.idiomatic: Seize their stores, march in triumph, and Pyongyang cannot stand."

sentences.zh: 群臣亦言：「張亮兵在沙城，召之信宿可至，乘高麗兇懼，並力拔烏骨城，渡鴨綠水，直取平壤，在此舉矣。」

translations.literal: The ministers also said: "Zhang Liang's troops are at Shacheng; summon them and they can arrive within two nights. Seize the moment while Goguryeo is terrified, take Wugu City together, cross the Yalu River, and strike straight for Pyongyang—this is the decisive move."
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers agreed: "Zhang Liang is at Shacheng—a messenger could bring him in two days. Strike while Goguryeo reels, take Wugu, cross the Yalu, and seize Pyongyang—now is the moment."

sentences.zh: 上將從之，獨長孫無忌以為：「天子親征，異於諸將，不可乘危徼幸。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to agree; only Zhangsun Wuji held that "the Son of Heaven campaigning in person is different from the generals—one cannot court danger for a lucky stroke.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was inclined to agree, but Zhangsun Wuji alone objected: "The Son of Heaven on campaign is not like a general—he must not gamble on a risky stroke.

sentences.zh: 今建安、新城之虜，眾猶十萬，若向烏骨，皆躡吾後，不如先破安市，取建安，然後長驅而進，此萬全之策也。」

translations.literal: The enemy at Jian'an and Xincheng still number a hundred thousand; if we march on Wugu, all will follow at our heels. Better to break Anshi first, take Jian'an, then drive forward at full speed—this is the plan of complete safety."
translations.idiomatic: Jian'an and Xincheng still hold a hundred thousand men—they will harry our rear if we strike Wugu. Take Anshi and Jian'an first, then advance—that is the sure course."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor held back.

sentences.zh: 諸軍急攻安市，上聞城中雞彘聲，謂李世勣曰：「圍城積久，城中煙火日微，今雞彘甚喧，此必饗士，欲夜出襲我，宜嚴兵備之。」

translations.literal: The armies pressed the attack on Anshi. The Emperor heard chickens and pigs in the city and said to Li Shiji: "The siege has lasted long and the smoke and fires in the city grow daily fainter; now chickens and pigs are very noisy—they must be feasting the troops and intend a night sortie against us. The army should be strictly prepared."
translations.idiomatic: As the siege wore on, the Emperor heard chickens and pigs from the city and told Li Shiji, "Smoke over the city grows thin, yet the livestock are loud—they are feasting the men for a night attack. Stand ready."

sentences.zh: 是夜，高麗數百人縋城而下。

translations.literal: That night several hundred Goguryeo men let themselves down from the wall on ropes.
translations.idiomatic: That night several hundred Goguryeo soldiers rappelled down the wall.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，自至城下，召兵急擊，斬首數十級，高麗退走。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and went in person to the foot of the wall, summoned troops to attack swiftly, cut off several dozen heads, and the Goguryeo withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, the Emperor rode to the wall, called up troops, killed dozens, and drove the raiders back.

sentences.zh: 江夏王道宗督眾築土山於城東南隅，浸逼其城，城中亦增高其城以拒之。

translations.literal: Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong supervised the masses in building an earthen hill at the southeast corner of the city, pressing gradually against the wall; within the city they also raised their wall higher to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong had the men build an earthen mound at the southeast corner, inching toward the walls while the defenders raised their ramparts higher.

sentences.zh: 士卒分番交戰，日六、七合，沖車砲石，壞其樓堞，城中隨立木柵以塞其缺。

translations.literal: Soldiers fought in rotating shifts, six or seven clashes a day; battering rams and catapult stones broke the towers and parapets, and within the city they at once set up wooden palisades to block the gaps.
translations.idiomatic: Troops fought in relays, six or seven assaults a day. Rams and stones smashed the towers; the defenders threw up wooden palisades to plug every breach.

sentences.zh: 道宗傷足，上親為之針。

translations.literal: Daozong injured his foot; the Emperor personally needled it for him.
translations.idiomatic: Daozong hurt his foot, and the Emperor personally treated it with acupuncture.

sentences.zh: 築山晝夜不息，凡六旬，用功五十萬，山頂去城數丈，下臨城中，道宗使果毅傅伏愛將兵屯山頂以備敵。

translations.literal: Building the hill did not cease day or night for sixty days in all, with five hundred thousand man-days of labor; the hilltop was several zhang from the city and overlooked it below. Daozong had the resolute officer Fu Fu'ai lead troops to camp on the summit against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: For sixty days the mound rose without pause—five hundred thousand man-days of labor—until its crest stood only yards above the wall. Daozong posted the officer Fu Fu'ai on the summit with a garrison.

sentences.zh: 山頹，壓城，城崩，會伏愛私離所部，高麗數百人從城缺出戰，遂奪據土山，塹而守之。

translations.literal: The hill collapsed, pressing against the city and breaking the wall; just then Fu'ai had left his command without permission, and several hundred Goguryeo came out through the breach to fight, seized the earthen hill, dug trenches, and held it.
translations.idiomatic: The mound collapsed onto the wall and breached it. Fu'ai had slipped away from his post, and hundreds of Goguryeo poured through the gap, recaptured the hill, and entrenched there.

sentences.zh: 上怒，斬伏愛以徇，命諸將攻之，三日不能克。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, executed Fu'ai as a public example, and ordered the generals to attack; for three days they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Fu'ai beheaded as an example and ordered an assault, but three days failed to retake the hill.

sentences.zh: 道宗徒跣詣旗下請罪，上曰：「汝罪當死，但朕以漢武殺王恢，不如秦穆用孟明，且有破蓋牟、遼東之功，故特赦汝耳。」

translations.literal: Daozong went barefoot to the command banner to beg punishment. The Emperor said: "Your crime deserves death, but I consider that Emperor Wu of Han killed Wang Hui whereas Duke Mu of Qin employed Meng Ming—and you have the merit of taking Gaimou and Liaodong, so I specially pardon you."
translations.idiomatic: Daozong came barefoot to accept blame. The Emperor said, "You deserve death, but killing you would be like Han Wudi executing Wang Hui when Duke Mu of Qin forgave Meng Ming—and you took Gaimou and Liaodong. I pardon you."

sentences.zh: 上以遼左早寒，草枯水凍，士馬難久留，且糧食將盡，癸未，敕班師。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because eastern Liaodong grows cold early, grass withers and water freezes, and troops and horses cannot long remain—and grain was nearly exhausted—on the day guiwei ordered withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Liaodong was already turning bitter cold; grass died, water froze, supplies ran low, and on the day guiwei the Emperor ordered the army home.

sentences.zh: 先拔遼、蓋二州戶口渡遼，乃耀兵於安市城下而旋，城中皆屏跡不出。

translations.literal: First the households of Liao and Gai prefectures were moved across the Liao River; then they displayed their might below Anshi City and turned back—the city kept all within and none came out.
translations.idiomatic: They resettled the people of Liao and Gai prefectures west of the river, paraded before Anshi, and withdrew while the city stayed silent behind its walls.

sentences.zh: 城主登城拜辭，上嘉其固守，賜縑百匹，以勵事君。

translations.literal: The city commandant mounted the wall to bow in farewell; the Emperor praised his stout defense, gave him a hundred bolts of silk, and thereby encouraged loyalty to one's lord.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant bowed from the wall in farewell. The Emperor admired his defense, gave him a hundred bolts of silk, and held him up as a model of loyalty.

sentences.zh: 命李世勣、江夏王道宗將步騎四萬為殿。

translations.literal: He ordered Li Shiji and Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong to lead forty thousand infantry and cavalry as the rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji and Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong commanded forty thousand infantry and cavalry as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，至遼東。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, they reached Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou they reached Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，渡遼水。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, they crossed the Liao River.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu they crossed the Liao River.

sentences.zh: 遼澤泥潦，車馬不通，命長孫無忌將萬人，剪草填道，水深處以車為梁，上自系薪於馬鞘以助役。

translations.literal: The Liao marshes were mud and flood; carts and horses could not pass. He ordered Zhangsun Wuji to lead ten thousand men to cut grass and fill the road; where the water was deep they used carts as bridges, and the Emperor himself tied firewood to his horse's saddle to help the work.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao marshes were impassable mire. Zhangsun Wuji led ten thousand men to cut reeds and fill the road, bridging deep water with carts while the Emperor lashed firewood to his saddle and labored alongside them.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙申朔，上至蒲溝駐馬，督填道諸軍渡渤錯水，暴風雪，士卒沾濕多死者，敕然火於道以待之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the first day bingchen, the Emperor reached Pugou and halted his horse, supervising the road-building armies crossing the Bohuo River. A violent wind and snow fell; many soldiers, soaked, died. He ordered fires lit along the road to await them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the new moon, he reached Pugou and oversaw the crossing of the Bohuo River. A blizzard killed many soaked soldiers; he ordered bonfires lit along the road to guide survivors in.

sentences.zh: 凡征高麗，拔玄菟、橫山、蓋牟、磨米、遼東、白巖、卑沙、麥谷、銀山、後黃十城，徙遼、蓋、巖三州戶口入中國者七萬人。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Goguryeo altogether they took ten cities—Xuantu, Hengshan, Gaimou, Momi, Liaodong, Baiyan, Beisha, Maigu, Yinshan, and Houhuang—and moved seventy thousand households from the three prefectures of Liao, Gai, and Yan into China.
translations.idiomatic: The Goguryeo campaign captured ten cities and resettled seventy thousand households from Liao, Gai, and Yan prefectures into the empire.

sentences.zh: 新城、建安、駐蹕三大戰，斬首四萬餘級，戰士死者幾二千人，戰馬死者什七、八。

translations.literal: In the three great battles at Xincheng, Jian'an, and Halting-the-Carriage, more than forty thousand heads were cut off; nearly two thousand warriors died, and seven or eight tenths of the war horses perished.
translations.idiomatic: Three major battles at Xincheng, Jian'an, and Halting-the-Carriage yielded forty thousand enemy heads; nearly two thousand Tang soldiers fell, and seven or eight tenths of the horses died.

sentences.zh: 上以不能成功，深悔之，歎曰：「魏徵若在，不使我有是行也！」

translations.literal: Because he had not achieved success, the Emperor deeply regretted it and sighed: "If Wei Zheng were still alive, he would not have let me make this expedition!"
translations.idiomatic: Unable to finish the conquest, the Emperor deeply regretted the campaign and sighed, "Had Wei Zheng lived, he would never have let me march!"

sentences.zh: 命馳驛祀征以少牢，復立所制碑，召其妻子詣行在，勞賜之。

translations.literal: He ordered post relays to sacrifice to Zheng with the lesser tai offering, re-erect the stele he had composed, and summon Zheng's wife and children to the imperial camp to be comforted and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He sent couriers to offer sacrifice to Wei Zheng, restored his memorial stele, and summoned the family to camp to honor them with gifts.

sentences.zh: 丙午，至營州。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, they reached Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingwu they reached Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔遼東戰亡士卒骸骨並集柳城東南，命有司設太牢，上自作文以祭之，臨哭盡哀。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the bones of soldiers who died in the Liaodong campaign gathered southeast of Liucheng; officials were commanded to set out the grand tai sacrifice, and the Emperor himself composed the text of the rite and wept over them to the full depth of grief.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the fallen of Liaodong gathered southeast of Liucheng, composed the funeral rite himself, and wept over them in full mourning.

sentences.zh: 其父母聞之，曰：「吾兒死而天子哭之，死何所恨！」

translations.literal: Their parents, hearing of it, said: "Our sons died and the Son of Heaven wept for them—what regret could death hold!"
translations.idiomatic: Their parents said, "Our sons died, yet the Son of Heaven mourned them—what more could we ask?"

sentences.zh: 上謂薛仁貴曰：「朕諸將皆老，思得新進驍勇者將之，無如卿者；

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Xue Rengui: "All my generals are old; I wish for a newly risen fierce and brave man to lead them—there is none like you;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Xue Rengui, "My generals are growing old. I need a young champion to lead them—and there is no one like you;

sentences.zh: 朕不喜得遼東，喜得卿也。」

translations.literal: I am not pleased at gaining Liaodong—I am pleased at gaining you."
translations.idiomatic: I am not glad for Liaodong—I am glad for you."

sentences.zh: 丙辰，上聞太子奉迎將至，從飛騎三千人馳入臨渝關，道逢太子。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, the Emperor heard the Crown Prince was coming to meet him and rode with three thousand flying cavalry into Linyu Pass, meeting the Crown Prince on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingchen, hearing the Crown Prince was coming to meet him, he galloped through Linyu Pass with three thousand cavalry and met the prince on the road.

sentences.zh: 上之發定州也，指所御褐袍謂太子曰：「俟見汝，乃易此袍耳。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor had set out from Ding Prefecture, he pointed to the brown robe he wore and told the Crown Prince: "When I see you, only then will I change this robe."
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Ding Prefecture he had pointed to his brown robe and told the prince, "I will not change this until I see you again."

sentences.zh: 在遼左，雖盛暑流汗，弗之易。

translations.literal: In eastern Liaodong, though the height of summer made him sweat, he did not change it.
translations.idiomatic: Through the heat of the Liaodong summer he never changed it.

sentences.zh: 及秋，穿敗，左右請易之，上曰：「軍士衣多弊，吾獨御新衣，可乎？」

translations.literal: When autumn came it was worn through; those around him asked to change it. The Emperor said: "The soldiers' clothes are mostly ragged—shall I alone wear new garments?"
translations.idiomatic: By autumn it was in tatters. His attendants urged a change, but he said, "My soldiers wear rags—should I alone dress in new clothes?"

sentences.zh: 至是，太子進新衣，乃易之。

translations.literal: Now the Crown Prince presented new clothes, and only then did he change.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the Crown Prince brought new robes did he finally change.

sentences.zh: 諸軍所虜高麗民萬四千口，先集幽州，將以賞軍士，上愍其父子夫婦離散，命有司平其直，悉以錢布贖為民，歡呼之聲，三日不息。

translations.literal: The fourteen thousand Goguryeo civilians captured by the armies had first been gathered at You Prefecture to be given as rewards to the soldiers; the Emperor pitied the separation of fathers and sons, husbands and wives, ordered officials to fix fair prices, and redeemed them all with cash and cloth to restore them as free people. Shouts of joy did not cease for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen thousand Goguryeo captives had been gathered at You Prefecture to reward the troops. Pitying their broken families, the Emperor paid fair prices and freed them all. Cheers rang out for three days.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛未，車駕至幽州，高麗民迎於城東，拜舞號呼，宛轉於地，塵埃彌望。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day xinwei, the imperial carriage reached You Prefecture; Goguryeo civilians welcomed it east of the city, bowing, dancing, and shouting, writhing on the ground until dust filled the view.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day xinwei, the court reached You Prefecture. Freed Goguryeo people welcomed them east of the city, kowtowing and weeping until dust obscured the sky.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，過易州境，司馬陳元□使民於地室蓄火種蔬而進之；

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, passing through Yi Prefecture, the marshal Chen Yuan[?] had the people store fire and grow vegetables in underground chambers to present them;
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengchen, passing Yi Prefecture, the marshal Chen Yuan had locals grow hot-house vegetables in underground pits to present to the court;

sentences.zh: 上惡其諂，免元□官。

translations.literal: the Emperor detested the flattery and dismissed Chen Yuan[?] from office.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor, disgusted by the flattery, stripped Chen Yuan of his post.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，車駕至定州。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, the imperial carriage reached Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day bingxu the court reached Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，吏部尚書楊師道坐所署用多非其才，左遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Minister of Personnel Yang Shidao, because many of those he had appointed were not men of talent, was demoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dinghai, Personnel Minister Yang Shidao was demoted to Minister of Works for appointing unqualified men.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，車駕發定州。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, the imperial carriage departed from Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renchen the court left Ding Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛丑，上病癰，御步輦而行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinchou, the Emperor suffered from a carbuncle and rode in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the day xinchou, the Emperor fell ill with an abscess and traveled in a litter.

sentences.zh: 戊申，至并州，太子為上吮癰，扶輦步從者數日。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, they reached Bing Prefecture; the Crown Prince sucked the pus from the carbuncle for the Emperor and walked beside the litter supporting it for several days.
translations.idiomatic: On the day wushen they reached Bing Prefecture. The Crown Prince sucked the pus from the abscess and walked beside the litter for days.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上疾瘳，百官皆賀。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, the Emperor's illness abated and all officials congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinhai the Emperor recovered, and the court rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 上之征高麗也，使右領軍大將軍執失思力將突厥屯夏州之北，以備薛延陀。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Goguryeo, he had Right Vanguard General Zhishi Sili lead Turks to encamp north of Xia Prefecture against the Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: For the Goguryeo campaign he had Right Vanguard General Zhishi Sili post Turks north of Xia Prefecture to guard against Xueyantuo.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀多彌可汗既立，以上出征未還，引兵寇河南，上遣左武候中郎將長安田仁會與思力合兵擊之。

translations.literal: After Qaghan Duomi of the Xueyantuo had been established, because the Emperor was on campaign and had not returned, he led troops to raid south of the Yellow River; the Emperor sent Left Martial Guard Commandant Tian Renhui of Chang'an to join Sili and strike him.
translations.idiomatic: The new Xueyantuo qaghan Duomi raided south of the Yellow River while the Emperor was away. The Emperor sent Left Martial Guard Commandant Tian Renhui to join Sili against him.

sentences.zh: 思力羸形偽退，誘之深入，及夏州之境，整陳以待之。

translations.literal: Sili feigned weakness and retreat, luring them deep in; when they reached the borders of Xia Prefecture he formed battle lines to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Sili feigned weakness and retreat, drew them deep, then formed battle lines at Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀大敗，追奔六百餘里，耀威磧北而還。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo were utterly defeated; pursuit ran more than six hundred li, and they displayed their might north of the desert before returning.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo were routed and pursued six hundred li; Tang power was displayed across the northern desert before the army returned.

sentences.zh: 多彌復發兵寇夏州，己未，敕禮部尚書江夏王道宗，發朔、並、汾、箕、嵐、代、忻、蔚、雲九州兵鎮朔州；

translations.literal: Duomi again sent troops to raid Xia Prefecture; on the day jiwei, an edict ordered Minister of Rites Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong to mobilize troops from the nine prefectures of Shuo, Bing, Fen, Ji, Lan, Dai, Xin, Yu, and Yun to garrison Shuo Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Duomi raided Xia Prefecture again. On the day jiwei the Emperor ordered Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong to mobilize troops from nine prefectures to garrison Shuo;

sentences.zh: 右衛大將軍代州都督薛萬徹，左驍衛大將軍阿史那社爾，發勝、夏、銀、綏、丹、延、鄜、坊、石、隰十州兵鎮勝州；

translations.literal: Right Guard General and Governor of Dai Prefecture Xue Wanche and Left Martial Guard General Ashina She'er were to mobilize troops from the ten prefectures of Sheng, Xia, Yin, Sui, Dan, Yan, Fu, Fang, Shi, and Xi to garrison Sheng Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Right Guard General Xue Wanche and Left Martial Guard General Ashina She'er were to garrison Sheng with troops from ten prefectures;

sentences.zh: 勝州都督宋君明，左武候將軍薛孤吳，發靈、原、寧、鹽、慶五州兵鎮靈州；

translations.literal: Governor of Sheng Prefecture Song Junming and Left Martial Guard General Xue Guwu were to mobilize troops from the five prefectures of Ling, Yuan, Ning, Yan, and Qing to garrison Ling Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Governor Song Junming and General Xue Guwu were to garrison Ling with troops from five prefectures;

sentences.zh: 又令執失思力發靈、勝二州突厥兵，與道宗等相應。

translations.literal: Zhishi Sili was also ordered to mobilize Turkic troops from Ling and Sheng prefectures to coordinate with Daozong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishi Sili was also to mobilize Turkic troops from Ling and Sheng to coordinate with them.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀至塞下，知有備，不敢進。

translations.literal: When the Xueyantuo reached the border, knowing there were preparations, they did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Xueyantuo reached the frontier, saw the defenses, and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 初，上留侍中劉洎輔皇太子於定州，仍兼左庶子、檢校民部尚書，總吏、禮、戶部三尚書事。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Emperor had left Palace Attendant Liu Ji to assist the Crown Prince at Ding Prefecture, who also served as Left Vice Heir Apparent and Acting Minister of the Household, overseeing the three ministries of Personnel, Rites, and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had left Palace Attendant Liu Ji at Ding Prefecture to assist the Crown Prince, also serving as vice heir-apparent and acting household minister over Personnel, Rites, and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 上將行，謂洎曰：「我今遠征，爾輔太子，安危所寄，宜深識我意。」

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to depart, he said to Ji: "I now campaign far away; you assist the Crown Prince—on you the safety and peril rest. You should deeply grasp my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he told Ji, "I march far away. You guard the Crown Prince—the realm's safety rests on you. Understand my intent fully."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「願陛下無憂，大臣有罪者，臣謹即行誅。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I wish Your Majesty no worries; if any great minister is guilty, your servant will at once carry out execution."
translations.idiomatic: Ji answered, "Have no fear, Your Majesty—if any minister offends, I will execute him at once."

sentences.zh: 上以其言妄發，頗怪之，戒曰：「卿性疏而太健，必以此敗，深宜慎之！」

translations.literal: The Emperor, because his words were rashly spoken, was rather displeased and warned him: "Your nature is loose and too bold—you will surely fail through this. You must be deeply cautious!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was troubled by his rashness and warned, "You are loose and overbold—you will destroy yourself this way. Be careful!"

sentences.zh: 及上不豫，洎從內出，色甚悲懼，謂同列曰：「疾勢如此，聖躬可憂！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor fell ill, Ji came out from within looking very mournful and afraid, and said to his colleagues: "The illness is thus—His Sacred Person is to be worried over!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor fell ill, Ji emerged from the inner quarters pale with fear and told his colleagues, "The illness is grave—the Son of Heaven is in danger!"

sentences.zh: 或譖於上曰：「洎言國家事不足憂，但當輔幼主行伊、霍故事，大臣有異志者誅之，自定矣。」

translations.literal: Someone slandered him to the Emperor, saying: "Ji said state affairs were not worth worrying over—one need only assist the young lord in the manner of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, execute great ministers with divergent intent, and all would settle itself."
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered him, claiming Ji had said state affairs did not matter—only to aid the young emperor like Yi Yin and Huo Guang and kill disloyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 上以為然，庚申，下詔稱：「洎與人竊議，窺窬萬一，謀執朝衡，自處伊、霍，猜忌大臣，皆欲夷戮。

translations.literal: The Emperor believed it; on the day gengshen he issued an edict stating: "Ji privately discussed with others, watching for a chance in ten thousand, plotting to seize the court's balance, placing himself as Yi and Huo, suspecting great ministers and wishing to exterminate them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor believed it. On the day gengshen he decreed that Ji had plotted treason, sought to rule as regent like Yi Yin and Huo Guang, and intended to slaughter the ministers.

sentences.zh: 宜賜自盡，免其妻孥。」

translations.literal: He should be granted suicide; his wife and children are spared."
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take his own life; his family was spared."

sentences.zh: 中書令馬周攝吏部尚書，以四時選為勞，請復以十一月選，至三月畢；

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Director Ma Zhou acted as Minister of Personnel; because selection in all four seasons was burdensome, he requested that selection again begin in the eleventh month and finish by the third;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat Director Ma Zhou, acting as personnel minister, found year-round appointments burdensome and asked to hold selections from the eleventh month through the third;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 是歲，右親衛中郎將裴行方討茂州叛羌黃郎弄，大破之，窮其餘黨，西至乞習山，臨弱水而歸。

translations.literal: That year, Right Personal Guard Commandant Pei Xingfang attacked the rebel Qiang Huang Langnong of Maozhou, defeated him utterly, pursued the remnant factions west to Mount Qixi, came to the Ruoshui River, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That year Right Personal Guard Commandant Pei Xingfang crushed the rebel Qiang leader Huang Langnong of Maozhou, pursued his remnants west to Mount Qixi and the Ruoshui River, and returned.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛未，夏州都督喬師望、右領軍大將軍執失思力等擊薛延陀，大破之，虜獲二千餘人。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinwei, Governor of Xia Prefecture Qiao Shiwang, Right Vanguard General Zhishi Sili, and others attacked the Xueyantuo and defeated them greatly, capturing more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on the day xinwei, Qiao Shiwang, Zhishi Sili, and others routed the Xueyantuo and took more than two thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 多彌可汗輕騎遁走，部內騷然矣。

translations.literal: Qaghan Duomi fled on light horse; within his tribes there was great unrest.
translations.idiomatic: Qaghan Duomi fled with a small escort, and his tribes fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，遣大理卿孫伏伽等二十二人以六條巡察四方，刺史、縣令以下多所貶黜，其人詣闕稱冤者，前後相屬。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, he sent Court of Judicial Review Director Sun Fuga and twenty-two others to inspect the four quarters by the six principles; many prefects and magistrates and below were demoted or dismissed, and those who came to the palace claiming injustice followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingchou he sent Sun Fuga and twenty-two inspectors on a six-point tour of the empire. Many local officials were demoted, and a stream of the wrongly punished came to appeal at court.

sentences.zh: 上令褚遂良類狀以聞，上親臨決，以能進擢者二十人，以罪死者七人，流以下除免者數百千人。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Chu Suiliang sort the cases and report; the Emperor personally decided them—twenty men of ability were promoted, seven were executed for crime, and several hundred or thousand were exiled, dismissed, or removed.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang summarized the cases for him. The Emperor judged personally: twenty capable men were promoted, seven executed, and hundreds demoted or exiled.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙未，上發并州。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yiyi, the Emperor departed from Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the day yiyi, the Emperor left Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三月，己巳，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jisi, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day jisi, the court returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上謂李靖曰：「吾以天下之眾困於小夷，何也？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Li Jing: "With the hosts of the realm I am bogged down by a petty barbarian people—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Li Jing, "How could the empire's full might be stalemated by a petty barbarian state?"

sentences.zh: 靖曰：「此道宗所解。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "This is what Daozong explained."
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing answered, "Prince Daozong explained it."

sentences.zh: 上顧問江夏王道宗，具陳在駐驊時乘虛取平壤之言。

translations.literal: The Emperor turned to ask Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong, who fully set forth his words at Halting-the-Carriage about seizing the moment to take Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor turned to Prince Jiangxia Li Daozong, who recounted his proposal at Halting-the-Carriage to strike Pyongyang while the enemy was exposed.

sentences.zh: 上悵然曰：「當時匆匆，吾不憶也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said regretfully: "At the time things were hurried—I do not recall it."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said wistfully, "I was too hurried then—I had forgotten."

sentences.zh: 上疾未全平，欲專保養，庚午，詔軍國機務並委皇太子處決。

translations.literal: The Emperor's illness was not yet fully healed; wishing to devote himself to recuperation, on the day gengwu he decreed that military and state affairs alike be entrusted to the Crown Prince for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Still recovering, on the day gengwu he entrusted all military and civil affairs to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 於是太子間日聽政於東宮，既罷，則入侍藥膳，不離左右。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Crown Prince on alternate days heard government at the Eastern Palace; when finished he would enter to attend medicines and meals, never leaving the Emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince heard cases every other day at the Eastern Palace, then returned to nurse the Emperor without leaving his side.

sentences.zh: 上命太子暫出遊觀，太子辭不願出；

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the Crown Prince to go out briefly for sightseeing; the Crown Prince declined and did not wish to go;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor urged the prince to take a brief outing, but the prince refused;

sentences.zh: 上乃置別院於寢殿側，使太子居之。

translations.literal: the Emperor then set up a separate courtyard beside the sleeping hall and had the Crown Prince dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: so the Emperor built a side chamber next to his sickroom for the prince.

sentences.zh: 褚遂良請遣太子旬日一還東宮，與師傅講道義；

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang requested that the Crown Prince every ten days return once to the Eastern Palace to discuss the Way and righteousness with his tutors;
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang asked that the prince return to the Eastern Palace every ten days to study with his tutors;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 上嘗幸未央宮，辟仗已過，忽於草中見一人帶橫刀，詰之，曰：「聞辟仗至，懼不敢出，辟仗者不見，遂伏不敢動。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once visited Weiyang Palace; the guard of honor had already passed when suddenly in the grass he saw a man wearing a horizontal blade. He questioned him; the man said: "Hearing the guard of honor arrive, I was afraid and did not dare come out; when the guard of honor was not seen, I lay hidden and did not dare move."
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Weiyang Palace after the honor guard had passed, the Emperor found a man with a sword hiding in the grass. The man said he had lain there in terror throughout the procession, afraid to move.

sentences.zh: 上遽引還，顧謂太子：「茲事行之，則數人當死，汝於後速縱遣之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor hastily led him back and, turning to the Crown Prince, said: "If this matter were carried through, several men would have to die—you afterward quickly release and send him away."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor hurried him away and told the Crown Prince, "If we pursued this, several men would die—release him quickly afterward."

sentences.zh: 又嘗乘腰輿，有三衛誤拂御衣，其人懼，色變。

translations.literal: Again, once riding in a waist litter, three guards of the Three Guards accidentally brushed the imperial robe; the man was afraid and his color changed.
translations.idiomatic: Once in a litter, a guard accidentally brushed the imperial robe; the man went pale with fear.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此間無御史，吾不汝罪也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Here there is no censor—I will not punish you."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "There is no censor here—I will not punish you."

sentences.zh: 陝人常德玄告刑部尚書張亮養假子五百人，與術士公孫常語，云「名應圖讖」，又問術士程公穎云：「吾臂有龍鱗起，欲舉大事，可乎？」

translations.literal: Chang De'xuan of Shan reported that Minister of Justice Zhang Liang kept five hundred foster sons and spoke with the adept Gongsun Chang, saying "his name matches the chart and prophecy," and also asked the adept Cheng Gongying: "Dragon scales have risen on my arm—I wish to raise a great affair; is it possible?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang De'xuan of Shan accused Justice Minister Zhang Liang of keeping five hundred foster sons and consulting adepts who said his name fulfilled prophecy. Liang had asked another adept whether dragon scales on his arm meant he should rebel.

sentences.zh: 上命馬周等按其事，亮辭不服。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Ma Zhou and others to investigate the matter; Liang argued but would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Ma Zhou and his colleagues investigate; Zhang Liang denied the charges and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「亮有假子五百人，養此輩何為？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Liang has five hundred foster sons—why raise this crowd?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Why keep five hundred foster sons?

sentences.zh: 正欲反耳！」

translations.literal: He plainly intends rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: He means to rebel!"

sentences.zh: 命百官議其獄，皆言亮反，當誅。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to deliberate the case; all said Liang had rebelled and should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the court to deliberate; all agreed Liang had rebelled and must die.

sentences.zh: 獨將作少匠李道裕言：「亮反形未具，罪不當死。」

translations.literal: Only Master of Works Assistant Li Daoyu said: "Liang's signs of rebellion are not yet complete; the crime does not warrant death."
translations.idiomatic: Only Master of Works aide Li Daoyu dissented: "The evidence of rebellion is incomplete—death is not warranted."

sentences.zh: 上遣長孫無忌、房玄齡就獄與亮訣曰：「法者天下之平，與公共之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Zhangsun Wuji and Fang Xuanling to the prison to take leave of Liang, saying: "Law is the balance of the realm—we share it with you.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Zhangsun Wuji and Fang Xuanling to bid Liang farewell: "Law is the empire's balance, and we share it with you.

sentences.zh: 公自不謹，與凶人往還，陷入於法，今將奈何！

translations.literal: You yourself were not cautious, consorted with evil men, and fell into the law—what is to be done now!
translations.idiomatic: You were careless, consorted with villains, and fell under the law—what can be done now?

sentences.zh: 公好去。」

translations.literal: Go well."
translations.idiomatic: Farewell."

sentences.zh: 己丑，亮與公穎俱斬西市，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: On jichou, Liang and Gongying were together beheaded at the Western Market, and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: On that day Zhang Liang and Cheng Gongying were both executed at the Western Market, and their estates were seized.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，刑部侍郎缺，上命執政妙擇其人，擬數人，皆不稱旨，既而曰：「朕得其人矣。

translations.literal: After more than a year the office of Vice Minister of Justice was vacant; the Emperor ordered the chief ministers carefully to choose a man; several were proposed, none pleasing his intent; eventually he said: "I have found the man.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later, with the vice ministership of Justice vacant, the Emperor asked his chief ministers to find the right man. Several candidates displeased him until he declared that he had found his man.

sentences.zh: 往者李道裕議張亮獄云『反形未具』，此言當矣，朕雖不從，至今悔之。」

translations.literal: Formerly Li Daoyu in deliberating Zhang Liang's case said 'the signs of rebellion were not yet complete'—that remark was correct; though I did not follow it, I regret it to this day."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Daoyu said Zhang Liang's rebellion was not yet fully proven, he was right. I rejected him then and have regretted it ever since."

sentences.zh: 遂以道裕為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Thereupon Daoyu was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daoyu was then appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 閏月，癸巳朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the first day guisi of the cycle, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, at the new moon on guisi day, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，罷遼州都督府及巖州。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Liaozhou Grand Protectorate and Yan Prefecture were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day the Liaozhou protectorate and Yan Prefecture were abolished.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子，太子太保蕭瑀解太保，乃同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiazi, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Xiao Yu was relieved of the grand mentor post and became again Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on jiazi day, Xiao Yu stepped down as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and resumed his post as chief councilor of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲寅，高麗王藏及莫離支蓋金遣使謝罪，並獻二美女，上還之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiayin, King Jang of Goguryeo and Molich Gai Jin sent envoys to express regret, also presenting two beautiful women; the Emperor returned them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiayin day, Goguryeo's King Jang and Minister Gai Jin of Molich sent envoys to apologize and offered two women; the Emperor sent them back.

sentences.zh: 金，即蘇文也。

translations.literal: "Jin" is Yeon Gaesomun.
translations.idiomatic: Gai Jin was Yeon Gaesomun.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁卯，西突闕乙毘射匱可汗遣使入貢，且請婚；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on dingmao, the Western Türk Yabgu Qaghan Shotpo Kulug sent envoys to offer tribute and also requested marriage;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on dingmao day, the Western Türk qaghan Shotpo Kulug sent tribute and asked for an imperial marriage alliance;

sentences.zh: 上許之，且使割龜茲、于闐、疏勒、朱俱波、蔥嶺五國以為聘禮。

translations.literal: the Emperor granted it and moreover had him cede the five states of Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, Zhuqubo, and Congling as betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor agreed and required him to yield Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, Zhuqubo, and the Congling region as the bride-price.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀多彌可汗，性褊急，猜忌無恩，廢棄父時貴臣，專用己所親暱，國人不附。

translations.literal: Duomi Qaghan of Xueyantuo was by nature narrow and hasty, suspicious and without grace; he cast aside his father's eminent ministers and used only those he personally favored; the people of the state did not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Duomi, qaghan of the Xueyantuo, was impulsive, suspicious, and ungrateful; he dismissed his father's ministers and favored only cronies, and his people lost heart.

sentences.zh: 多彌多所誅殺，人不自安。

translations.literal: Duomi executed many; men did not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: His executions spread fear through the realm.

sentences.zh: 回紇酋長吐迷度與僕骨、同羅共擊之，多彌大敗。

translations.literal: The Uyghur chieftain Tumidu together with Pugu and Tongluo jointly attacked him; Duomi was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur chief Tumidu allied with the Pugu and Tongluo to strike him, inflicting a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔以江夏王道宗、左衛大將軍阿史那社爾為瀚海安撫大使；

translations.literal: On yihai, an edict appointed Prince Daizong of Jiangxia and Grand General of the Left Guard Ashina She'er as Commissioners for Pacification of Hanhai;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day the Emperor named Prince Daizong of Jiangxia and Left Guard general Ashina She'er commissioners to pacify the Hanhai region;

sentences.zh: 又遣右領衛大將軍執失思力將突厥兵，右驍衛大將軍契苾何力將涼州及胡兵，代州都督薛萬徹、營州都督張儉各將所部兵，分道並進，以擊薛延陀。

translations.literal: furthermore he sent Right Colonel of the Leading Guard Zhisi Sili to lead Türk troops, Right Colonel of the Valiant Cavalry Qibi Heli to lead Liangzhou and barbarian troops, and Dai Prefecture Protector Xue Wanche and Ying Prefecture Protector Zhang Jian each to lead their departmental troops, advancing by separate routes together to strike Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: and dispatched Zhisi Sili with Türk cavalry, Qibi Heli with Liangzhou and tribal forces, and Xue Wanche and Zhang Jian with their own commands in a coordinated advance against Xueyantuo.

sentences.zh: 上遣校尉宇文法詣烏羅護、靺鞨，遇薛延陀阿波設之兵於東境，法帥靺鞨擊破之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Commandant Yuwen Fa to go to Wuluo Guard and Mohe; he encountered Xueyantuo Apo She's troops on the eastern frontier; Fa led the Mohe and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Commandant Yuwen Fa to the Wuluo Guard and Mohe peoples. On the eastern frontier Fa met Apo She's Xueyantuo force and routed it with Mohe allies.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀國中驚擾，曰：「唐兵至矣！」

translations.literal: Within Xueyantuo's state there was alarm and disturbance; they said: "Tang troops have arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through Xueyantuo: "The Tang army is upon us!"

sentences.zh: 諸部大亂。

translations.literal: The various tribes fell into great disorder.
