translations.idiomatic: Every tribe broke into chaos.

sentences.zh: 多彌引數千騎奔阿史德時健部落，回紇攻而殺之，並其宗族殆盡，遂據其地。

translations.literal: Duomi led several thousand horsemen to flee to the tribe of Ashide Shijian; the Uyghurs attacked and killed him, and almost entirely extirpated his clan, then occupied his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Duomi fled with a few thousand riders to the Ashide Shijian tribe; the Uyghurs pursued, killed him, nearly wiped out his clan, and seized his lands.

sentences.zh: 諸俟斤互相攻擊，爭遣使來歸命。

translations.literal: The various irkins attacked one another and vied in sending envoys to submit to imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal leaders fought each other while rushing envoys to pledge allegiance to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀餘眾西走，猶七萬餘口，共立真珠可汗兄子咄摩支為伊特勿失可汗，歸其故地。

translations.literal: The remaining multitudes of Xueyantuo fled west; there were still more than seventy thousand mouths; together they installed Zhenzhu Qaghan's nephew Duomozhi as Yite Wushi Qaghan and returned to their former lands.
translations.idiomatic: Some seventy thousand Xueyantuo survivors fled west, enthroned Duomozhi—a nephew of the late qaghan Zhenzhu—as Yite Wushi Qaghan, and resettled their old pastures.

sentences.zh: 尋去可汗之號，遣使奉表，請居郁督軍山之北；

translations.literal: Soon he removed the qaghan title, sent envoys presenting a memorial, and requested to dwell north of Yudujun Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: He soon renounced the qaghan title, petitioned the court, and asked to settle north of Mount Yudujun;

sentences.zh: 使兵部尚書崔敦禮就安集之。

translations.literal: the Emperor sent Minister of War Cui Dunli to go and settle and assemble them.
translations.idiomatic: and sent War Minister Cui Dunli to receive and settle them.

sentences.zh: 敕勒九姓酋長，以其部落素服薛延陀種，聞咄摩支來，皆恐懼，朝議恐其為磧北之患，乃更遣李世勣與九姓敕勒共圖之。

translations.literal: The chieftains of the nine surnames of the Tiele, because their tribes had long submitted to the Xueyantuo stock, on hearing Duomozhi's coming were all afraid; the court deliberated, fearing he would become a trouble north of the desert, and so again sent Li Shiji together with the nine-surname Tiele to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele chieftains of nine clans, long subject to Xueyantuo rule, feared Duomozhi's return. Court officials worried about renewed trouble beyond the desert and sent Li Shiji with the nine Tiele tribes to deal with him.

sentences.zh: 上戒世勣曰：「降則撫之，叛則討之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor admonished Shiji, saying: "If they submit, pacify them; if they rebel, punish them."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor instructed Li Shiji: "Accept surrender with kindness; crush rebellion with force."

sentences.zh: 己丑，上手詔，以「薛延陀破滅，其敕勒諸部，或來降附，或未歸服，今不乘機，恐貽後悔，朕當自詣靈州招撫。

translations.literal: On jichou, the Emperor's personal edict stated: "Xueyantuo has been destroyed and broken; among the Tiele tribes some have come to submit and attach, some have not yet returned to allegiance—if we do not seize this opportunity, I fear we will leave regret; I shall myself go to Lingzhou to summon and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the Emperor issued a personal edict: "With Xueyantuo destroyed, many Tiele tribes have submitted while others remain aloof. This moment must not be lost to regret—I will go to Lingzhou myself to win them over.

sentences.zh: 其去歲征遼東兵，皆不調發。」

translations.literal: The troops conscripted last year for the Liaodong campaign will all not be mobilized."
translations.idiomatic: None of last year's Liaodong expedition forces would be mobilized for the journey."

sentences.zh: 時太子當從行，少詹事張行成上疏，以為：「皇太子從幸靈州，不若使之監國，接對百寮，明習庶政，既為京師重鎮，且示四方盛德。

translations.literal: At that time the Crown Prince was to accompany the journey; Junior Tutor Zhang Xingcheng submitted a memorial, holding: "If the Crown Prince accompanies the visit to Lingzhou, it would be better to have him oversee the state, meet and respond to the hundred officials, clearly learn diverse administration—both as the capital's great safeguard and to display flourishing virtue to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was slated to accompany the tour when Junior Tutor Zhang Xingcheng submitted a memorial arguing that he should remain as regent, meet the officials, learn governance, guard the capital, and display imperial steadiness to the empire.

sentences.zh: 宜割私愛，俯從公道。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to cut off private affection and bow to follow the public way."
translations.idiomatic: Put private feeling aside and follow the public good."

sentences.zh: 上以為忠，進位銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor regarded this as loyal and advanced him in rank to Silver Glory Grand Master of Splendid Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his loyalty and promoted him to Silver Glory Grand Master of Splendid Hall.

sentences.zh: 李世勣至郁督軍山，其酋長梯真達官帥眾來降。

translations.literal: Li Shiji reached Yudujun Mountain; its chieftain Tizhen daguan led the multitude to submit.
translations.idiomatic: At Yudujun Mountain, Li Shiji received the surrender of chieftain Tizhen Daguan and his people.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀咄摩支南奔荒谷，世勣遣通事舍人蕭嗣業往招慰，咄摩支詣嗣業降。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo's Duomozhi fled south into a wild valley; Shiji sent Interpreter-scribe Xiao Siye to go summon and comfort him; Duomozhi came to Siye and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Duomozhi fled south into the wilds; Li Shiji sent Xiao Siye to treat with him, and Duomozhi surrendered to Siye.

sentences.zh: 其部落猶持兩端，世勣縱兵追擊，前後斬五千餘級，虜男女三萬餘人。

translations.literal: His tribe still held to both sides; Shiji released troops in pursuit; before and after more than five thousand heads were cut off, and men and women captives numbered more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His tribe still wavered, so Li Shiji attacked, killing more than five thousand and capturing over thirty thousand men and women.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，咄摩支至京師，拜右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Duomozhi reached the capital; he was appointed Grand General of the Right Guard of Martial Might.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Duomozhi reached the capital and was made Grand General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 八月，甲子，立皇孫忠為陳王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on jiazi, the imperial grandson Zhong was established as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on jiazi day, the Emperor's grandson Zhong was created Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 己巳，上行幸靈州。

translations.literal: On jisi, the Emperor traveled in felicity to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day the Emperor set out for Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 江夏王道宗兵既渡磧，遇薛延陀阿波達官眾數萬拒戰，道宗擊破之，斬首千餘級，追奔二百里。

translations.literal: After Prince Daizong of Jiangxia's troops had crossed the sands, they encountered tens of thousands of Xueyantuo Apo Daguan's multitude resisting battle; Daizong defeated them, cutting off more than a thousand heads and pursuing the fugitives two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daizong crossed the desert, smashed a Xueyantuo force tens of thousands strong under Apo Daguan, took more than a thousand heads, and pursued them two hundred li.

sentences.zh: 道宗與薛萬徹各遣使招諭敕勒諸部，其酋長皆喜，頓首請入朝。

translations.literal: Daizong and Xue Wanche each sent envoys to summon and instruct the various Tiele tribes; their chieftains were all pleased and knocked their heads requesting to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong and Xue Wanche sent envoys to the Tiele tribes, whose chieftains gladly knocked their heads and asked to come to court.

sentences.zh: 庚午，車駕至浮陽。

translations.literal: On gengwu, the imperial carriage reached Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day the imperial procession reached Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 回紇、拔野古、同羅、僕骨、多濫葛、思結、阿跌、契苾、跌結、渾、斛薛等十一姓各遣使入貢，稱：「薛延陀不事大國，暴虐無道，不能與奴等為主，自取敗死，部落鳥散，不知所之。

translations.literal: The eleven surnames—Uyghur, Bayegu, Tongluo, Pugu, Duolangge, Sijie, Adiva, Qibi, Diejie, Hun, and Husue—each sent envoys to offer tribute, stating: "Xueyantuo did not serve the great state, was violent and tyrannical without the Way, could not be lord to us slaves—he brought defeat and death on himself; the tribes scattered like birds, not knowing whither.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven tribal confederations including the Uyghurs and Bayegu sent tribute, declaring that Xueyantuo had refused to serve the great power, ruled with cruelty, and deserved ruin; their clans had fled like startled birds.

sentences.zh: 奴等各有分地，不從薛延陀去，歸命天子。

translations.literal: We slaves each have our allotted lands, did not follow Xueyantuo in departure, and return our lives to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We keep our own lands and have not followed Xueyantuo; we submit to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 願賜哀憐，乞置官司，養育奴等。」

translations.literal: We wish to be granted pity and compassion, begging that official agencies be established to nurture us slaves."
translations.idiomatic: Grant us mercy and appoint officials to care for us."

sentences.zh: 上大喜。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 辛未，詔回紇等使者宴樂，頒賚拜官，賜其酋長璽書；

translations.literal: On xinwei, an edict had the Uyghur and other envoys feasted with music, rewards conferred and offices granted, and seal letters bestowed on their chieftains;
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day he feasted the tribal envoys, gave rewards and titles, and granted sealed patents to their chieftains;

sentences.zh: 遣右領軍中郎將安永壽報使。

translations.literal: Right Central Battalion Leader of the Leading Guard An Yongshou was sent as returning envoy.
translations.idiomatic: and dispatched An Yongshou of the Right Leading Guard as envoy in reply.

sentences.zh: 壬申，上幸漢故甘泉宮，詔以「戎、狄與天地俱生，上皇並列，流殃構禍，乃自運初。

translations.literal: On renshen, the Emperor visited the former Han Ganquan Palace; an edict stated: "Barbarians and Di were born together with Heaven and Earth, ranking beside the august sovereigns; spreading calamity and forging disaster has been so from the beginning of fate.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he visited the old Han Ganquan Palace and proclaimed: "Since creation the northern peoples have stood beside the sage kings, yet from the dawn of history they have brought war and ruin.

sentences.zh: 朕聊命偏師，遂擒頡利；

translations.literal: I merely ordered a flank army and thus captured Jieli;
translations.idiomatic: With a single detachment I captured Jieli;

sentences.zh: 始弘廟略，已滅延陀。

translations.literal: at the beginning I displayed the temple strategy and already destroyed Yantuo.
translations.idiomatic: and by imperial design have now destroyed the Xueyantuo.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒百餘萬戶，散處北溟，遠遣使人，委身內屬，請同編列，並為州郡；

translations.literal: More than a million households of the Tiele, scattered in the northern sea, sent envoys from afar, entrusted their persons and came within submission, requesting to be registered together and all made into prefectures and districts;
translations.idiomatic: Over a million Tiele households beyond the northern sea have sent envoys to submit and ask to be registered as Tang prefectures;

sentences.zh: 混元以降，殊未前聞，宜備禮告廟，仍頒示普天。」

translations.literal: since the Grand Primal beginning, this has notably not been heard before; it is fitting to prepare ritual and report to the temples, and still promulgate and show to all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: such a thing has never been known since the world's beginning. Let full rites be reported to the ancestral temples and the tidings proclaimed to all the realm."

sentences.zh: 庚辰，至涇州；

translations.literal: On gengchen, he reached Jing Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he arrived at Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，逾隴山，至西瓦亭，觀馬牧。

translations.literal: On bingxu, he crossed Long Mountain, reached West Wa Pavilion, and viewed horse pastures.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu he crossed Long Mountain to West Wa Pavilion to inspect the horse herds.

sentences.zh: 九月，上至靈州，敕勒諸部俟斤遣使相繼詣靈州者數千人，鹹云：「願得天至尊為奴等天可汗，子子孫孫常為天至尊奴，死無所恨。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the Emperor reached Lingzhou; the irkins of the various Tiele tribes sent envoys in succession to Lingzhou, numbering several thousand persons; all said: "We wish to obtain the Heavenly August Sovereign as our Heavenly Qaghan; generation after generation we shall always be slaves of the Heavenly August Sovereign—even in death we have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he reached Lingzhou, where thousands of Tiele envoys pledged: "Make us your Heavenly Qaghan; we and our descendants will serve you forever without regret."

sentences.zh: 甲辰，上為詩序其事曰：「雪恥酬百王，除凶報千古。」

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Emperor composed a poem narrating the affair, saying: "Snow shame requites the hundred kings; remove the vicious, repay the thousand ages."
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day he composed a poem on the event: "White shame pays the hundred kings; ending evil answers the ages."

sentences.zh: 公卿請勒石於靈州；

translations.literal: The dukes and ministers requested that stone be carved at Lingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: His ministers asked that the occasion be carved in stone at Lingzhou;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 特進同中書門下三品宋公蕭瑀，性狷介，與同寮多不合，嘗言於上曰：「房玄齡與中書門下眾臣，朋黨不忠，執權膠固。

translations.literal: Privileged Attendant Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank Duke of Song Xiao Yu was by nature narrow and principled; with colleagues he mostly did not agree; he once said to the Emperor: "Fang Xuanling and the Secretariat and Chancellery multitude form a partisan clique disloyal, clutching power rigidly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, Duke of Song and chief councilor, was touchy and quarrelsome with colleagues. He once told the Emperor that Fang Xuanling and the chancellery formed a disloyal faction monopolizing power.

sentences.zh: 陛下不詳知，但未反耳。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not thoroughly know—they have only not yet rebelled."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty does not see it clearly—they have simply not rebelled yet."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言得無太甚！

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Are your words not rather too extreme!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "Is that not going too far?

sentences.zh: 人君選賢才以為股肱心膂，當推誠任之。

translations.literal: A ruler selects worthy talent to be his arms and thighs, heart and backbone—he should extend sincerity and entrust them.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler chooses able men as his arms and his heart and must trust them fully.

sentences.zh: 人不可以求備，必捨其所短，取其所長。

translations.literal: One cannot demand completeness in a person; one must set aside his shortcomings and take his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: No man is flawless; overlook faults and employ strengths.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不能聰明，何至頓迷臧否，乃至於是！」

translations.literal: Though I am not able to be intelligent, how would I suddenly be deluded about good and bad, even to this point!"
translations.idiomatic: I may not be brilliant, but I am not so blind to right and wrong as that!"

sentences.zh: 瑀內不自得，既數忤旨，上亦銜之，但以其忠直居多，未忍廢也。

translations.literal: Yu inwardly was ill at ease; having repeatedly defied the imperial intent, the Emperor also harbored resentment, but because his straightforwardness was mostly the greater part, he could not yet bear to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu grew uneasy. Though the Emperor resented his repeated defiance, he still tolerated him for his habitual blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂張亮曰：「卿既事佛，何不出家？」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said to Zhang Liang: "You already serve the Buddha—why not leave home?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once said to him, "You are devoted to Buddhism—why not become a monk?"

sentences.zh: 瑀因自請出家。

translations.literal: Yu thereupon himself requested to leave home.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu promptly asked permission to take orders.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「亦知公雅好桑門，今不違公意。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I also know you greatly favor śramanas; now I do not go against your intent."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I know your love for the monastic life and will not oppose you."

sentences.zh: 瑀須臾復進曰：「臣適思之，不能出家。」

translations.literal: After a moment Yu again advanced and said: "Your subject has just considered it—I cannot leave home."
translations.idiomatic: Moments later Xiao Yu returned and said, "On reflection, I cannot become a monk."

sentences.zh: 上以瑀對群臣發言反覆，尤不能平；

translations.literal: The Emperor because Yu before the host of ministers spoke words back and forth was especially unable to be appeased;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was especially displeased that Xiao Yu had contradicted himself before the court;

sentences.zh: 會稱足疾不朝，或至朝堂而不入見。

translations.literal: coincidentally he claimed foot ailment and did not attend court, or reached the court hall but did not enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: and Xiao Yu then pleaded foot trouble, either absenting himself or lingering in the hall without audience.

sentences.zh: 上知瑀意終怏怏，冬，十月，手詔數其罪曰：「朕於佛教，非意所遵。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew Yu's mind was ultimately discontented; in winter, the tenth month, a personal edict enumerated his crimes, saying: "I toward Buddhism am not intentionally devoted.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Xiao Yu remained resentful, in the tenth month of winter the Emperor's personal edict listed his offenses: "Buddhism is not what I intend to follow.

sentences.zh: 求其道者未驗福於將來，修其教者翻受辜於既往。

translations.literal: Those who seek its Way have not verified blessings in what is to come; those who cultivate its teaching on the contrary receive guilt in what is past.
translations.idiomatic: Its promise of future blessing goes unproved; its devotees suffer guilt for the past.

sentences.zh: 至若梁武窮心於釋氏，簡文銳意於法門，傾帑藏以給僧示氐，殫人力以供塔廟。

translations.literal: As for Liang Wu exhausting his heart on Śākya's clan, Jianwen sharpening his purpose on the Dharma gate, pouring treasury stores to supply the monk Shi Shi, exhausting human strength to supply pagodas and temples.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang poured his soul into Buddhism and Emperor Jian of Liang into the Dharma, emptying the treasury for monks and conscripting labor for temples.

sentences.zh: 及乎三淮沸浪，五嶺騰煙，假餘息於熊蹯，引殘魂於雀鷇，子孫覆亡而不暇，社稷俄頃而為墟，報施之征，何其謬也！

translations.literal: When the three Huai boiled with waves and the five Ridges rose with smoke, borrowing remaining breath in bear's paws, drawing lingering souls in sparrow nests—descendants perished without leisure, and altars of state in an instant became ruins; the signs of recompense—how very mistaken!
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai seethed and the Lingnan burned, their scions perished and their states fell in moments—what blind reward was that!

sentences.zh: 瑀踐覆車之餘軌，襲亡國之遺風；

translations.literal: Yu tread the ruts after an overturned cart and inherited the remnant wind of perished states;
translations.idiomatic: You follow the wheel tracks of ruined realms and their dying customs;

sentences.zh: 棄公就私，未明隱顯之際；

translations.literal: abandoned the public to pursue the private, not clarifying the boundary between hidden and manifest;
translations.idiomatic: you abandoned public duty for private ends, blind to what should be shown or concealed;

sentences.zh: 身俗口道，莫辨邪正之心。

translations.literal: body worldly but mouth preaching the Way, unable to distinguish the mind of evil and right.
translations.idiomatic: you lived as a layman while preaching the Way, unable to tell evil from right.

sentences.zh: 修累葉之殃源，祈一躬之福本，上以違忤君主，下則扇習浮華。

translations.literal: You cultivated the source of calamity for accumulated generations and prayed for the root of blessing for one person alone—above you defied and offended the ruler, below you fanned and taught frivolous display.
translations.idiomatic: You courted multigenerational misfortune for private blessing, defying your sovereign above while spreading vain fashion below.

sentences.zh: 自請出家，尋復違異。

translations.literal: You yourself requested to leave home and soon again went against it.
translations.idiomatic: You asked to take orders, then at once refused.

sentences.zh: 一回一惑，在乎瞬息之間；

translations.literal: One turn, one confusion—in the space between a wink and a breath;
translations.idiomatic: Conviction and doubt traded places in a breath;

sentences.zh: 自可自否，變於帷扆之所。

translations.literal: self-assent, self-denial—changing within the place of curtain and throne.
translations.idiomatic: you affirmed and denied yourself before the imperial throne.

sentences.zh: 乖棟樑之體，豈具瞻之量乎！

translations.literal: You betray the substance of a pillar and beam—how could you possess the measure of one whom all look up to!
translations.idiomatic: You have failed as a pillar of state—what leader can the court look up to?

sentences.zh: 朕隱忍至今，瑀全無悛改。

translations.literal: I have restrained myself until today; Yu entirely has no change of heart.
translations.idiomatic: I have borne with you until now, yet you show no repentance.

sentences.zh: 可商州刺史，仍除其封。」

translations.literal: He may be made Prefect of Shang Prefecture, and his enfeoffment is likewise removed."
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to prefect of Shangzhou and stripped of his fief."

sentences.zh: 上自高麗還，蓋蘇文益驕恣，雖遣使奉表，其言率皆詭誕；

translations.literal: After Emperor Taizong returned from Goryeo, Yeon Gaesomun grew all the more arrogant and unrestrained; though he sent envoys to present a memorial, their words were for the most part deceitful and absurd;"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong returned from his Goryeo campaign, Yeon Gaesomun grew bolder; though he sent envoys with memorials, their words were mostly lies;"

sentences.zh: 又待唐使者倨慢，常窺伺邊隙。

translations.literal: Moreover he treated Tang envoys with arrogance and slowness, and constantly spied for openings along the border.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Tang envoys with contempt and constantly watched for weaknesses along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 屢敕令勿攻新羅，而侵陵不止。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he was ordered by edict not to attack Silla, yet his encroachments never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeatedly forbidden to attack Silla, he kept raiding without stop.

sentences.zh: 壬申，詔勿受其朝貢，更議討之。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, an edict was issued not to accept their tribute, and to deliberate again on punishing them.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day the court refused their tribute and debated renewed punitive action.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己丑，上以幸靈州往還，冒寒疲頓，欲於歲前專事保攝。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jichou: because Emperor Taizong in going to and returning from Lingzhou had braved cold and was weary and exhausted, he wished before year's end to devote himself solely to preserving his health.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on jichou, Emperor Taizong—exhausted by the cold journey to and from Lingzhou—resolved to rest and recuperate before year's end.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己丑，詔祭祀、表疏、胡客、兵馬、宿衛，行魚契給驛、授五品以上官及除解、決死罪皆以聞，餘並取皇太子處分。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, jichou: an edict [said that] sacrifices, memorials, barbarian guests, troops and horses, palace guards, issuing fish tallies and relay stations, appointing officials of fifth rank and above and removals and dismissals, and deciding capital crimes—all were to be reported [to the Emperor]; the rest were all to be decided by the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jichou, Emperor Taizong reserved sacrifices, memorials, foreign visitors, troops, guards, travel tallies, senior appointments, dismissals, and capital sentences for himself; everything else went to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己丑，群臣累請封禪；

translations.literal: Twelfth month, jichou: the host of ministers repeatedly requested the feng and shan rites;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jichou, the ministers repeatedly petitioned for the Mount Tai rites;

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: [He] assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔造羽衛送洛陽宮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the imperial guards constructed and sent to Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the imperial guard prepared and sent to the Luoyang palace.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，回紇俟利發吐迷度、僕骨俟利發歌濫拔延、多濫葛俟斤末、拔野古俟利發屈利失、同羅俟利發時健啜、思結酋長烏碎及渾、斛薛、奚結、阿跌、契苾、白□酋長皆來朝。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, the Uyghur yabghu Tulumidu, the Bokut yabghu Gelanboyan, the Dolange irkin Mo, the Bayegu yabghu Qulishi, the Tongluo yabghu Shijianchuo, the Sijie chieftain Wusui, and the chieftains of Hun, Huoxue, Xijie, Adie, Qibi, and Bai□ all came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day the Uyghur, Bokut, Dolange, Bayegu, Tongluo, and Sijie leaders, with chiefs of the Hun, Huoxue, Xijie, Adie, Qibi, and Bai□ tribes, all presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，上賜宴於芳蘭殿，命有司厚加給待，每五日一會。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Emperor Taizong bestowed a banquet in the Hall of Fragrant Orchids, ordering the relevant offices to give them generous provisions and entertainment, with a gathering every five days.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Emperor Taizong feasted them in the Hall of Fragrant Orchids, ordering lavish provisions and a gathering every five days.

sentences.zh: 癸未，上謂長孫無忌等曰：「今日吾生日，世俗皆為樂，在朕翻成傷感。

translations.literal: On the day guimwei, Emperor Taizong said to Zhangsun Wuji and the others: "Today is my birthday; the world all take it for joy, but in me it instead becomes poignant grief.
translations.idiomatic: On guimwei Emperor Taizong told Zhangsun Wuji and the others, "Today is my birthday. The world celebrates, but for me it only deepens sorrow.

sentences.zh: 今君臨天下，富有四海，而承歡膝下，永不可得，此子路所以有負米之恨也。

translations.literal: Now I lord over all under Heaven and possess the four seas, yet to bring joy beneath my parents' knees is forever unattainable—this is why Zilu had the regret of carrying rice.
translations.idiomatic: I rule the realm and own the four seas, yet I can never again delight my parents at their knee—that is why Zilu mourned that he could no longer carry rice for them.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『哀哀父母，生我劬勞。』

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Alas, alas, my parents—who bore me with toil and weariness.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, 'Alas for my parents, who bore me with such labor.'

sentences.zh: 奈何以劬勞之日更為宴樂乎！」

translations.literal: How then on a day of toil and weariness can we make it a feast and revelry!'
translations.idiomatic: How can I turn a day that should honor their labor into feasting and pleasure!"

sentences.zh: 因泣數行下，左右皆悲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept, tears streaming down several lines; those at his side were all grieved."
translations.idiomatic: He wept until tears ran down his face, and all those beside him were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡嘗以微譴歸第，褚遂良上疏，以為：「玄齡自義旗之始翼贊聖功，武德之季冒死決策，貞觀之初選賢立政，人臣之勤，玄齡為最。

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling once because of a slight reproof returned to his residence; Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial, holding that: "From the beginning of the righteous banner Xuanling aided and supported the sage achievement; in the late Wude period he braved death in decision-making; in the early Zhenguan period he selected the worthy and established government—among ministers in diligence, Xuanling was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling had once been sent home over a minor rebuke. Chu Suiliang memorialized that from the founding of the dynasty through Wude and into Zhenguan, Fang Xuanling's service had been unmatched among ministers.

sentences.zh: 自非有罪在不赦，搢紳同尤，不可遐棄。

translations.literal: Unless there is offense within unpardonable guilt and the gentry share the blame alike, he cannot be cast off to a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Unless his crime is unpardonable and the court shares the blame, he must not be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 陛下若以其衰老，亦當諷諭使之致仕，退之以禮；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty considers him aged, you should also admonish and instruct him to retire from office and dismiss him with ceremony;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty thinks him too old, you should counsel him to retire and send him off with honor;

sentences.zh: 不可以淺鮮之過，棄數十年之勳舊。」

translations.literal: you cannot because of a shallow and slight fault abandon a meritorious elder of several decades."
translations.idiomatic: not discard decades of merit over a trifling fault.

sentences.zh: 上遽召出之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong immediately summoned him forth."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong at once recalled him to court.

sentences.zh: 頃之，玄齡復避位還家。

translations.literal: Before long, Xuanling again yielded his post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Fang Xuanling again resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 久之，上幸芙蓉園，玄齡敕子弟汛掃門庭，曰：「乘輿且至！」

translations.literal: After a long while, Emperor Taizong visited Furong Garden; Xuanling ordered his sons and younger kin to rinse and sweep the gate and courtyard, saying: "The imperial carriage is about to arrive!"
translations.idiomatic: Some time later, when Emperor Taizong visited Furong Garden, Fang Xuanling had his household sweep the courtyard, saying, "The emperor is coming!"

sentences.zh: 有頃，上果幸其第，因載玄齡還宮。

translations.literal: Before long, Emperor Taizong indeed visited his residence, and thereupon carried Xuanling back to the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after, the emperor did visit his home and took him back to the palace in the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，開府儀同三司申文獻公高士廉疾篤；

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Pillar of State with Honored Parity of the First Rank, Duke of Shen and Literary Accomplishment Gao Shilian was gravely ill;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Grand Mentor Gao Shilian, Duke of Shen, fell gravely ill;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上幸其第，流涕與訣；

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Emperor Taizong visited his residence, weeping as he took leave;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Emperor Taizong visited him, weeping as he said farewell;

sentences.zh: 壬辰，薨。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he died.

sentences.zh: 上將往哭之，房玄齡以上疾新愈，固諫，上曰：「高公非徒君臣，兼以故舊姻戚，豈得聞其喪不往哭乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was about to go to mourn him; Fang Xuanling because Emperor Taizong's illness had newly healed firmly remonstrated; Emperor Taizong said: "Lord Gao is not merely minister and ruler—we are also old friends and kin by marriage; how can I hear of his bereavement and not go to weep?
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong prepared to attend the funeral, Fang Xuanling, citing his recent recovery, urged him not to go. The emperor said, "Lord Gao was not only my minister but an old friend and kinsman—how can I hear of his death and not mourn him?

sentences.zh: 公勿復言！」

translations.literal: Sir, speak no more!"
translations.idiomatic: Say no more!"

sentences.zh: 帥左右自興安門出。

translations.literal: He led his attendants out through Xing'an Gate."
translations.idiomatic: He led his attendants out through Xing'an Gate.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌在士廉喪所，聞上將至，輟哭，迎諫於馬首曰：「陛下餌金石，於方不得臨喪，奈何不為宗廟蒼生自重！

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji was at Shilian's mourning hall; hearing Emperor Taizong was coming, he stopped weeping and met him to remonstrate at his horse's head, saying: "Your Majesty takes mineral elixirs; by prescription you must not attend funerals—how can you not value yourself for the sake of the ancestral temple and the black-haired people!
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji was at the mourning hall. Hearing the emperor was coming, he stopped weeping and blocked his horse, saying, "Your Majesty takes elixirs and by medical rule must not attend funerals—will you not spare the state and the people this risk?

sentences.zh: 且臣舅臨終遺言，深不欲以北首、夷衾，輒屈鑾駕。」

translations.literal: Moreover my maternal uncle's dying testament deeply did not wish that with head to the north and barbarian covers the imperial carriage should be bent to come."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover my uncle's dying wish was that the imperial carriage should not come to find him laid out head north under foreign covers."

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong would not listen."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 無忌中道伏臥，流涕固諫，上乃還入東苑，南望而哭，涕下如雨。

translations.literal: Wuji midway prostrated himself, weeping as he firmly remonstrated; Emperor Taizong then returned into the Eastern Park, looked south and wept, tears falling like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji threw himself down in the road, weeping and pleading until the emperor turned back into the Eastern Park, gazed south, and wept until tears fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 及柩出橫橋，上登長安故城西北樓，望之慟哭。

translations.literal: When the bier passed out through Heng Bridge, Emperor Taizong ascended the northwest tower of Chang'an's old city wall and gazed upon it, wailing in grief.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin crossed Heng Bridge, he climbed the northwest tower of old Chang'an and wailed as he watched it pass.

sentences.zh: 丙申，詔以回紇部為瀚海府，僕骨為金微府，多濫葛為燕然府，拔野古為幽陵府，同羅為龜林府，思結為盧山府，渾為皋蘭州，斛薛為高闕州，奚結為雞鹿州，阿跌為雞田州，契苾為榆溪州，思結別部為蹛林州，白□為置顏州；

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, an edict made the Uyghur tribe Hanhai Prefecture, the Bokut Jinwei Prefecture, the Dolange Yanshan Prefecture, the Bayegu Youling Prefecture, the Tongluo Guilin Prefecture, the Sijie Lushan Prefecture, the Hun Gaolan Prefecture, the Huoxue Gaoque Prefecture, the Xijie Jilu Prefecture, the Adie Jitian Prefecture, the Qibi Yuxi Prefecture, a separate Sijie division Dunlin Prefecture, and Bai□ Zhiyan Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen the court established prefectures for the Uyghur, Bokut, Dolange, Bayegu, Tongluo, Sijie, Hun, Huoxue, Xijie, Adie, Qibi, a separate Sijie branch, and Bai□ tribes;

sentences.zh: 各以其酋長為都督、刺史，各賜金銀繒帛及錦袍。

translations.literal: each with its chieftain as protector-general or prefect, each bestowed gold, silver, silks, and brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: appointed each chieftain governor or prefect, and bestowed gold, silver, silks, and brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 敕勒大喜，捧戴歡呼拜舞，宛轉塵中。

translations.literal: The Tiele were greatly pleased, lifting [the gifts] on high, shouting in joy, bowing and dancing, writhing in the dust.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele were overjoyed, shouting, bowing, and dancing as they rolled in the dust.

sentences.zh: 及還，上御天成殿宴，設十部樂而遣之。

translations.literal: When they returned, Emperor Taizong held court at Tiancheng Hall with a banquet, set out the ten-section music, and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: On their departure Emperor Taizong feasted them in Tiancheng Hall with the ten-section orchestra and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 諸酋長奏稱：「臣等既為唐民，往來天至尊所，如詣父母，請於回紇以南、突厥以北開一道，謂之參天可汗道，置六十八驛，各有馬及酒肉以供過使，歲貢貂皮以充租賦，仍請能屬文人，使為表疏。」

translations.literal: The various chieftains memorialized, saying: "We are already Tang people; in coming and going to the Heaven-Sovereign's place it is like visiting parents. We request that south of the Uyghur and north of the Turks a road be opened, called the Road of the Khan of Heaven Who Reaches the Sky, with sixty-eight relay stations, each with horses and wine and meat to supply passing envoys; yearly tribute of sable pelts to serve as land tax; and we still request literati skilled in composition to draft our memorials."
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs petitioned: "We are now subjects of Tang; visiting the Son of Heaven is like visiting our parents. We ask for a road south of the Uyghur and north of the Turks—the Road of the Heaven-Reaching Khan—with sixty-eight relay stations stocked with horses, wine, and meat for envoys, yearly sable tribute in lieu of tax, and literati to write our memorials."

sentences.zh: 上皆許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong granted all of it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong granted every request.

sentences.zh: 於是北荒悉平，然回紇吐迷度已私自稱可汗，官號皆如突厥故事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the northern wilds were all pacified; yet the Uyghur Tulumidu had already on his own called himself khan, and official titles all followed the Turkic precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The northern frontier was thus pacified, though Uyghur leader Tulumidu had already styled himself khan with Turkic titles.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔以明年仲春有事泰山，禪社首；

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, an edict [said that] in the mid-spring of next year there would be the rite at Mount Tai, with the shan at Mount Sheshou;
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou the court scheduled the Mount Tai feng and Sheshou shan rites for the following mid-spring;

sentences.zh: 餘並依十五年議。

translations.literal: the rest all followed the deliberations of the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: all other arrangements followed the plan of the fifteenth year.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁丑，太子釋奠於國學。

translations.literal: Second month, day dingchou: the Crown Prince performed the libation sacrifice at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingchou, the crown prince offered the ceremonial libation at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 上將復伐高麗，朝議以為：「高麗依山為城，攻之不可猝拔。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong was about to campaign against Goryeo again; court deliberation held that: "Goryeo relies on mountains for its cities; attacking them cannot be suddenly taken.
translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Taizong prepared another Goryeo campaign, the court argued that Goryeo's mountain fortresses could not be taken quickly.

sentences.zh: 前大駕親征，國人不得耕種，所克之城，悉收其谷，繼以旱災，民太半乏食。

translations.literal: Earlier the great carriage personally campaigned; the people could not plant or harvest; every city taken had all its grain collected; followed by drought disaster—the people for the most part lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: The last imperial campaign had kept farmers from their fields, stripped grain from captured towns, and drought had left most of the people hungry.

sentences.zh: 今若數遣偏師，更迭擾其疆場，使彼疲於奔命，釋耒入堡，數年之間，千里蕭條，則人心自離，鴨綠之北，可不戰而取矣。」

translations.literal: Now if we repeatedly send detached columns to take turns harassing their borderlands, making them weary from rushing to answer, laying down ploughs to enter forts—in several years' time a thousand li will be desolate; then hearts will of themselves turn away, and north of the Yalu can be taken without battle."
translations.idiomatic: Send detachments in rotation to harry their borders until they exhaust themselves, abandon the fields, and crowd into forts. In a few years a thousand li will lie waste, the people will turn against their rulers, and everything north of the Yalu may be won without a major battle.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong followed this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 三月，以左武衛大將軍牛進達為青丘道行軍大總管，右武候將軍李海岸副之，發兵萬餘人，乘樓船自萊州泛海而入。

translations.literal: Third month: the General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guards Niu Jinda was made Grand Commander of the Qingqiu Route Army, the General of the Right Martial Guards Li Hai'an as his deputy; more than ten thousand troops were raised, boarding tower ships from Laizhou to cross the sea and enter.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Niu Jinda, general of the Left Martial Guards, was made grand commander of the Qingqiu route with Li Hai'an as deputy; they raised more than ten thousand men and entered by sea from Laizhou in tower ships.

sentences.zh: 又以太子詹事李世勣為遼東道行軍大總管，右武衛將軍孫貳朗等副之，將兵三千人，因營州都督府兵自新城道入。

translations.literal: Also the Crown Prince's Household Steward Li Shiji was made Grand Commander of the Liaodong Route Army, the General of the Right Martial Guards Sun Erlang and others as deputies; he led three thousand troops, and relying on the Bingzhou Protectorate troops entered by the Xincheng route.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiji, steward of the crown prince's household, was made grand commander of the Liaodong route with Sun Erlang and others as deputies; with three thousand men he entered by the Xincheng route supported by Bingzhou garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 兩軍皆選習水善戰者配之。

translations.literal: Both armies all selected men skilled in water and good at fighting to be assigned to them.
translations.idiomatic: Both forces were staffed with men skilled in naval combat.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，上曰：「朕於戎、狄所以能取古人所不能取，臣古人所不能臣者，皆順眾人之所欲故也。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Emperor Taizong said: "I toward the Rong and Di am able to take what men of old could not take and make subjects of what men of old could not make subjects—all because I follow what the multitude desire.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Emperor Taizong said, "I have won and ruled peoples the ancients could not because I follow what they themselves want.

sentences.zh: 昔禹帥九州之民，鑿山槎木，疏百川注之海，其勞甚矣，而民不怨者，因人之心，順地之勢，與民同利故也。」

translations.literal: In old times Yu led the people of the Nine Provinces, cut through mountains and set rafts of wood, dredged the hundred streams to pour into the sea—the toil was very great, yet the people did not resent it, because he followed men's hearts, complied with the land's configuration, and shared benefit with the people."
translations.idiomatic: Yu led the Nine Provinces to cut mountains, raft timber, and channel rivers to the sea. The labor was immense, yet the people did not complain because he followed their hearts, suited the terrain, and shared the benefit."

sentences.zh: 是月，上得風疾，苦京師盛暑，夏，四月，乙丑，命修終南山太和廢宮為翠微宮。

translations.literal: That month Emperor Taizong contracted wind ailment and suffered from the capital's intense summer heat; summer, fourth month, day yichou: he ordered the abandoned Taihe Palace on Mount Zhongnan restored as Cuiwei Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That month Emperor Taizong fell ill with a wind disorder and, distressed by the capital's summer heat, ordered in the fourth month on yichou that the abandoned Taihe Palace on Mount Zhongnan be restored as Cuiwei Palace.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，置燕然都護府，統瀚海等六都督、皋蘭等七州，以揚州都督府司馬李素立為之。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, the Yanran Protectorate was established, governing the six protectorates such as Hanhai and the seven prefectures such as Gaolan; Yangzhou Protectorate Senior Administrator Li Suli was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Yanran Protectorate was established over six protectorates including Hanhai and seven prefectures including Gaolan, with Li Suli of Yangzhou as its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 素立撫以恩信，夷落懷之，共率馬牛為獻；

translations.literal: Suli comforted them with kindness and trust; the barbarian settlements cherished him and together led horses and cattle as offerings;
translations.idiomatic: Suli won them with kindness and trust, and the tribes brought horses and cattle as gifts;

sentences.zh: 素立唯受其酒一杯，餘悉還之。

translations.literal: Suli accepted from each only one cup of wine and returned all the rest.
translations.idiomatic: he accepted only one cup of wine from each and returned the rest.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊子，上幸翠微宮。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuzi: Emperor Taizong visited Cuiwei Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on wuzi, Emperor Taizong went to Cuiwei Palace.

sentences.zh: 冀州進士張昌齡獻《翠微宮頌》，上愛其文，命於通事舍人裡供奉。

translations.literal: Jizhou presented scholar Zhang Changling offered "Ode to Cuiwei Palace"; Emperor Taizong loved its writing and ordered him attached in service within the Secretariat for Matters of Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Changling of Jizhou presented an ode to Cuiwei Palace; pleased with it, the emperor attached him to the secretariat for protocol service.

sentences.zh: 初，昌齡與進士王公治皆善屬文，名振京師，考功員外郎王師旦知貢舉，黜之，舉朝莫曉其故。

translations.literal: Earlier Changling and the presented scholar Wang Gongzhi were both skilled at literary composition; their names shook the capital; the Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel Wang Shidan oversaw the examinations and rejected them—the whole court did not understand the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Changling and Wang Gongzhi were famed in the capital for their writing, yet Wang Shidan, chief examiner, failed them and no one knew why.

sentences.zh: 及奏第，上怪無二人名，詰之。

translations.literal: When the examination rolls were submitted, Emperor Taizong wondered at the absence of the two men's names and questioned it.
translations.idiomatic: When the results were announced, the emperor noticed their absence and demanded an explanation.

sentences.zh: 師旦對曰：「二人雖有辭華，然其體輕薄，終不成令器。

translations.literal: Shidan replied: "The two men though they have verbal brilliance, yet their substance is frivolous and light; in the end they will not become fine vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Shidan replied, "They are fluent writers, but their tone is frivolous and they will never become solid statesmen.

sentences.zh: 若置之高第，恐後進效之，傷陛下雅道。」

translations.literal: If placed in high rank, I fear later comers will imitate them and harm Your Majesty's refined Way."
translations.idiomatic: If promoted, later candidates would imitate them and harm Your Majesty's standards of taste."

sentences.zh: 上善其言。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong approved his words."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔百司依舊啟事皇太子。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, an edict [said that] the hundred offices should as before report affairs to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the court ordered all offices to resume reporting to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，上御翠微殿，問侍臣曰：「自古帝王雖平定中夏，不能服戎、狄。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Emperor Taizong held court at Cuiwei Hall and asked his attendant ministers: "From antiquity emperors and kings though they pacified central China could not subdue the Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, in Cuiwei Hall, Emperor Taizong asked his ministers, "Emperors of old might pacify China yet could not win over the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 朕才不逮古人而成功過之，自不諭其故，諸公各率意以實言之。」

translations.literal: My talent does not reach the men of old yet my achievement surpasses theirs—I myself do not understand the reason; each of you, speak frankly according to your mind and tell the truth."
translations.idiomatic: My talent falls short of the ancients, yet I have surpassed them, and I do not know why. Speak frankly and tell me the truth."

sentences.zh: 群臣皆稱：「陛下功德如天地，萬物不得而名言。」

translations.literal: The host of ministers all said: "Your Majesty's merit and virtue are like Heaven and earth; the ten thousand things cannot be named in words."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all said, "Your Majesty's merit is like Heaven and earth—beyond words."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 朕所以能及此者，止由五事耳。

translations.literal: The reason I am able to reach this is only through five matters.
translations.idiomatic: I have reached this point for only five reasons.

sentences.zh: 自古帝王多疾勝己者，朕見人之善，若己有之。

translations.literal: From antiquity emperors and kings mostly hated those who surpassed themselves; I see others' excellence as if I possessed it myself.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers often resented those who outshone them; when I see excellence in others, I take it as my own.

sentences.zh: 人之行能，不能兼備，朕常棄其所短，取其所長。

translations.literal: Men's conduct and ability cannot be fully combined; I constantly discard their shortcomings and take their strong points.
translations.idiomatic: No one combines every talent, so I set aside weaknesses and use strengths.

sentences.zh: 人主往往進賢則欲置諸懷，退不肖則欲推諸壑，朕見賢者則敬之，不肖者則憐之，賢不肖各得其所。

translations.literal: Rulers often when advancing the worthy wish to place them in their bosom, and when dismissing the unworthy wish to push them into gullies; I see the worthy then revere them, the unworthy then pity them—the worthy and unworthy each obtain their place.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers often embrace the worthy and cast the unworthy into the abyss; I honor the worthy and pity the unworthy, so each finds his place.

sentences.zh: 人主多惡正直，陰誅顯戮，無代無之，朕踐祚以來，正直之士，比肩於朝，未嘗黜責一人。

translations.literal: Rulers mostly hate the upright; hidden execution and open punishment exist in no age without them; since I ascended the throne, upright men stand shoulder to shoulder at court—I have never dismissed or reproached a single one.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers often hate the upright and destroy them in secret or in public; since my accession upright men have filled the court, and I have never punished one.

sentences.zh: 自古皆貴中華，賤夷、狄，朕獨愛之如一，故其種落皆依朕如父母。

translations.literal: From antiquity all have honored the central states and despised the Yi and Di; I alone love them as one; therefore their tribes all rely on me as on parents.
translations.idiomatic: All ages have prized China and despised the barbarians; I have loved them alike, and so their peoples cling to me as to parents.

sentences.zh: 此五者，朕所以成今日之功也。」

translations.literal: These five are why I have accomplished today's achievement."
translations.idiomatic: These five things account for what I have achieved today."

sentences.zh: 顧謂褚遂良曰：「公嘗為史官，如朕言，得其實乎？」

translations.literal: Turning, he said to Chu Suiliang: "You once served as historiographer—does what I say match the truth?"
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Chu Suiliang and said, "You were once a historiographer—is what I say true?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下盛德不可勝載，獨以此五者自與，蓋謙謙之志耳。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty's abundant virtue cannot be fully recorded; that you alone attribute it to these five matters is surely the intent of modest humility."
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang replied, "Your Majesty's virtue is beyond record; to reduce it to these five points shows modesty."

sentences.zh: 李世勣軍既渡遼，歷南蘇等數城，高麗多背城拒戰，世勣擊破其兵，焚其羅郭而還。

translations.literal: Li Shiji's army having crossed the Liao, passed through several cities such as Nansu; Goryeo mostly relied on their cities to resist battle; Shiji struck and broke their troops, burned their outer walls, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shiji's army crossed the Liao, it marched through Nansu and other towns; though Goryeo often fought from behind city walls, Shiji defeated their forces, burned the outer ramparts, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸亥，以司徒長孫無忌領揚州都督，實不之任。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day guihai: the Minister of Works Zhangsun Wuji was made concurrent Yangzhou Protector, but in fact did not go to the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guihai, Minister of Works Zhangsun Wuji was named Yangzhou protector but did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，詔以「隋末喪亂，邊民多為戎、狄所掠，今鐵勒歸化，宜遣使詣燕然等州，與都督相知，訪求沒落之人，贖以貨財，給糧遞還本貫；

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, an edict [said that] "In the Sui end there was mourning chaos; border people were mostly seized by the Rong and Di. Now the Tiele have submitted; envoys should be sent to the Yanran and other prefectures to coordinate with the protectors, seek out persons lost and fallen, redeem them with goods and wealth, supply grain and relays, and return them to their native districts;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou an edict declared that since the chaos at the end of Sui many border people had been taken by the tribes, and now that the Tiele had submitted, envoys should go to Yanran and other prefectures to find captives, ransom them, supply grain and escort, and return them home;

sentences.zh: 其室韋、烏羅護、靺鞨三部人為薛延陀所掠者，亦令贖還。」

translations.literal: those of the Shiwei, Wuluohu, and Mohe three groups seized by the Xueyantuo were also ordered redeemed and returned."
translations.idiomatic: those taken from the Shiwei, Wuluohu, and Mohe by the Xueyantuo were likewise to be ransomed and restored."

sentences.zh: 癸未，以司農卿李緯為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: On the day guimwei, the Minister of Agriculture Li Wei was made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On guimwei Li Wei, minister of agriculture, was appointed minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時房玄齡留守京師，有自京師來者，上問：「玄齡何言？」

translations.literal: At that time Fang Xuanling was left to guard the capital; someone came from the capital; Emperor Taizong asked: "What did Xuanling say?"
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling was then left in charge of the capital. When a messenger arrived, Emperor Taizong asked what Xuanling had said.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「玄齡聞李緯拜尚書，但雲李緯美髭鬢。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Xuanling heard Li Wei was appointed Minister and only said Li Wei has beautiful beard and whiskers."
translations.idiomatic: The messenger replied that Xuanling, hearing of Li Wei's appointment, had only remarked on his fine beard.

sentences.zh: 帝遽改除緯洛州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately changed Wei to Prefect of Luozhou."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once reassigned Li Wei to prefect of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，牛進達、李海岸入高麗境，凡百餘戰，無不捷。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Niu Jinda and Li Hai'an entered Goryeo territory; in all more than a hundred battles, none were not victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Niu Jinda and Li Hai'an entered Goryeo and fought more than a hundred engagements without a defeat.

sentences.zh: 攻石城，拔之。

translations.literal: They attacked Shicheng and took it.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed and captured Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 進至積利城下，高麗兵萬餘人出戰，海岸擊破之，斬首二千級。

translations.literal: Advancing to below Jili City, more than ten thousand Goryeo troops came out to fight; Hai'an struck and broke them, beheading two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: At Jili City more than ten thousand Goryeo troops came out; Li Hai'an routed them and took two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 上以翠微宮險隘，不能容百官，庚子，詔更營玉華宮於宜春之鳳皇谷。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong because Cuiwei Palace was cramped and narrow and could not accommodate the hundred offices, on the day gengzi ordered that Yuhua Palace be newly built in Yichun's Phoenix Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Cuiwei Palace too cramped for the full court, on gengzi Emperor Taizong ordered Yuhua Palace built in Phoenix Valley at Yichun.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬戌，詔以薛延陀新降，土功屢興，加以河北水災，停明年封禪。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day renxu: an edict [said that] because the Xueyantuo had newly submitted, earthworks were repeatedly raised, and moreover there was flooding disaster in Hebei, next year's feng and shan were halted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renxu, the court halted next year's Mount Tai rites because the Xueyantuo had just submitted, construction was constant, and Hebei had suffered floods.

sentences.zh: 辛未，骨利幹遣使入貢；

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Guligan sent envoys to present tribute;
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Guligan sent tribute envoys;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以骨利幹為玄闕州，拜其俟斤為刺史。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Guligan was made Xuanque Prefecture, and its irkin was appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Guligan was made Xuanque Prefecture and its leader appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 骨利幹於鐵勒諸部為最遠，晝長夜短，日沒後，天色正曛，煮羊脾適熟，日已復出矣。

translations.literal: Among the Tiele tribes Guligan was the most remote; days were long and nights short. After the sun set the sky was still twilight—by the time a sheep's spleen was boiled just done, the sun had risen again.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the Tiele confederations, Guligan lay farthest north, where summer days stretched on and nights scarcely came. After sunset the heavens still glowed like dusk; a sheep's spleen could finish boiling and the sun would already be climbing back.

sentences.zh: 己丑，齊州人段志衝上封事，請上致政於皇太子；

translations.literal: On jichou, Duan Zhichong of Qizhou submitted a sealed memorial asking the Emperor to transfer power to the Crown Prince;
translations.idiomatic: On the day jichou, Duan Zhichong of Qizhou presented a sealed memorial urging Emperor Taizong to abdicate in favor of the Crown Prince;

sentences.zh: 太子聞之，憂形於色，發言流涕。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince heard of it; worry showed on his face, and as he spoke he wept.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince heard this, grief showed plainly on his face and he burst into tears as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌等請誅志沖。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji and others asked that Zhichong be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji and others requested that Zhichong be put to death.

sentences.zh: 上手詔曰：「五嶽陵霄，四海亙地，納污藏疾，無損高深。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally issued an edict saying: "The Five Peaks pierce the clouds; the Four Seas span the earth—they receive filth and harbor illness, yet suffer no loss to their height and depth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong issued a personal edict: "The Five Sacred Peaks tower into the heavens; the Four Seas stretch across the earth—they absorb pollution and conceal sickness, yet their loftiness and depth are not diminished.

sentences.zh: 志沖欲以匹夫解位天子，朕若有罪，是其直也；

translations.literal: Zhichong wishes with a common man to relieve the Son of Heaven of his position—if We have guilt, that is his straightforwardness;
translations.idiomatic: If Zhichong, a commoner, would have the Son of Heaven yield his throne, then if We are guilty, that is his honest bluntness;

sentences.zh: 若其無罪，是其狂也。

translations.literal: if We are without guilt, that is his madness.
translations.idiomatic: if We are innocent, that is his madness.

sentences.zh: 譬如尺霧障天，不虧於大；

translations.literal: It is like a foot of mist blocking the sky—it does not diminish its vastness;
translations.idiomatic: It is like a span of mist veiling the sky—it does not lessen the heavens' breadth;

sentences.zh: 寸雲點日，何損於明！」

translations.literal: an inch of cloud spotting the sun—how does it harm its brightness!"
translations.idiomatic: a finger's breadth of cloud flecking the sun—what does it subtract from its radiance!"

sentences.zh: 丁酉，立皇子明為曹王。

translations.literal: On dingyou, the imperial son Ming was established as Prince of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: On the day dingyou, the Emperor's son Li Ming was created Prince of Cao.

sentences.zh: 明母楊氏，巢剌王之妃也，有寵於上；

translations.literal: Ming's mother Lady Yang was consort of Prince Chao of Cili and had the Emperor's favor;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ming's mother, Lady Yang, had been consort to Prince Chao of Cili and enjoyed Emperor Taizong's favor;

sentences.zh: 文德皇后之崩也，欲立為皇后。

translations.literal: At the death of Empress Wende, he wished to establish her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wende's death, he had wished to make her empress.

sentences.zh: 魏徵諫曰：「陛下方比德唐、虞，奈何以辰嬴自累！」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng remonstrated: "Your Majesty is just now comparing your virtue to Tang and Yu—how can you be burdened with Chen Ying!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng admonished, "Your Majesty sets his virtue against Yao and Shun—how can you let a Chen Ying drag you down!"

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 尋以明繼元吉後。

translations.literal: Before long Ming was made heir to Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Li Ming was made heir to Li Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，敕宋州刺史王波利等發江南十二州工人造大船數百艘，欲以征高麗。

translations.literal: On wuxu, an edict ordered Songzhou prefect Wang Boli and others to mobilize workers from twelve Jiangnan prefectures to build several hundred large ships, intending to use them against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, the court ordered Wang Boli, prefect of Songzhou, and others to levy craftsmen from twelve southern prefectures to build hundreds of great ships for a campaign against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚辰，奴剌啜匐俟友帥其所部萬餘人內附。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on gengchen, Futouyou of the Nuluo tribe led more than ten thousand of his people to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on gengchen, Futouyou of the Nulu tribe led his following of over ten thousand in submission.

sentences.zh: 十一月，突厥車鼻可汗遣使入貢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Türk qaghan Chebi sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Chebi, qaghan of the Turks, sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 車鼻名斛勃，本突厥同族，世為小可汗。

translations.literal: Chebi's name was Hubo; he was originally of the same clan as the Turks and for generations had been a minor qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: Chebi, personal name Hubo, was of the same Türk stock and for generations had held the rank of minor qaghan.

sentences.zh: 頡利之敗，突厥餘眾欲奉以為大可汗，時薛延陀方強，車鼻不敢當，帥其眾歸之。

translations.literal: When Jieli was defeated, the remaining Türks wished to install him as great qaghan; at that time the Xueyantuo were just powerful, and Chebi dared not accept, leading his people to submit to them.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli's defeat, the scattered Turks wanted to make him great qaghan, but Xueyantuo was then ascendant and Chebi dared not claim the title; he led his tribes to acknowledge them.

sentences.zh: 或說薛延陀：「車鼻貴種，有勇略，為眾所附，恐為後患，不如殺之。」

translations.literal: Someone urged the Xueyantuo: "Chebi is of noble blood, brave and resourceful, and the masses attach to him—we fear he will be a later trouble; better to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Some advised the Xueyantuo leaders, "Chebi is of the royal line, bold and skilled, and the people rally to him—he may become a threat later. Better kill him now."

sentences.zh: 車鼻知之，逃去。

translations.literal: Chebi learned of it and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Chebi learned of this, he fled.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀遣數千騎追之，車鼻勒兵與戰，大破之，乃建牙於金山之北，自稱乙注車鼻可汗，突厥餘眾稍稍歸之，數年間勝兵三萬人，時出抄掠薛延陀。

translations.literal: The Xueyantuo sent several thousand riders in pursuit; Chebi marshaled troops to fight them and routed them badly, then raised his royal tent north of the Altai, styling himself Yizhu Chebi Qaghan; Türk remnants gradually returned to him, and within a few years he had thirty thousand fighting men, sometimes raiding the Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo sent thousands of horsemen in pursuit; Chebi rallied his warriors, smashed them utterly, then pitched his camp north of the Altai Mountains as Yizhu Chebi Qaghan. Turk remnants drifted back to him until, within a few years, he commanded thirty thousand warriors and raided Xueyantuo whenever he could.

sentences.zh: 及薛延陀敗，車鼻勢益張，遣其子沙缽羅特勒入見，又請身自入朝。

translations.literal: When the Xueyantuo were defeated, Chebi's power grew still more; he sent his son Shaboluo tele to come in audience and also asked to enter court in person.
translations.idiomatic: After Xueyantuo fell, Chebi's strength swelled further. He sent his son Shaboluo Telle for an audience at court and asked to come himself.

sentences.zh: 詔遣將軍郭廣敬征之。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched General Guo Guangjing to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered General Guo Guangjing to march against him.

sentences.zh: 車鼻特為好言，初無來意，竟不至。

translations.literal: Chebi was especially good with words but from the first had no intent to come; in the end he did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Chebi spoke fair words but never meant to come, and in the end he stayed away.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，徙順陽王泰為濮王。

translations.literal: On guimao, Prince Shunyang Tai was moved to be Prince of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Li Tai was shifted from Prince of Shunyang to Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 壬子，上疾愈，三日一視朝。

translations.literal: On renzi, the Emperor's illness abated; every three days he attended court once.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Emperor Taizong recovered and began holding audience once every three days.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬申，西趙酋長趙磨帥萬餘戶內附，以其地為明州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renshen, the western Zhao chieftain Zhao Mo led more than ten thousand households to submit inward; his territory was made Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renshen, Zhao Mo, chieftain of Western Zhao, led over ten thousand households in submission, and his lands were organized as Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 龜茲王伐疊卒，弟訶黎布失畢立，浸失臣禮，侵漁鄰國。

translations.literal: The Kucha king Fadie died; his younger brother Helibushibi succeeded and gradually neglected ministerial courtesy, encroaching on and plundering neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Kucha, Fadie, died. His brother Helibushibi succeeded the throne, slowly abandoned tributary propriety, and preyed on neighboring realms.

sentences.zh: 上怒，戍寅，詔使持節、昆丘道行軍大總管、左驍衛大將軍阿史那社爾、副大總管、右驍衛大將軍契苾何力、安西都護郭孝恪等將兵擊之，仍命鐵勒十三州、突厥、吐蕃、吐谷渾連兵進討。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered; on wuyin, an edict appointed the envoy bearing the staff of authority, campaign commander of the Kunqiu route and Left Guard General Ashina She'er, deputy commander and Right Guard General Qibi Heli, Protector-General of Anxi Guo Xiaoke, and others to lead troops in an attack, and furthermore ordered the thirteen Tiele prefectures, the Turks, Tibet, and Tuyuhun to join forces in a linked advance.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Emperor Taizong on wuyin ordered Ashina She'er, Left Guard General and commander of the Kunqiu expedition, with his deputy Qibi Heli, Right Guard General, and Guo Xiaoke, Protector-General of Anxi, among others, to strike Kucha, and commanded the thirteen Tiele prefectures plus Turk, Tibetan, and Tuyuhun forces to advance in concert.

sentences.zh: 高麗王使其子莫離支任武入謝罪，上許之。

translations.literal: The Goguryeo king sent his son Molizhi Renwu to enter and beg forgiveness; the Emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Goguryeo sent his son Molizhi Renwu to court with apologies, and Emperor Taizong accepted.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己丑，上作《帝范》十二篇以賜太子，曰《君體》、《建親》、《求賢》、《審官》、《納諫》、《去讒》、《戒盈》、《崇儉》、《賞罰》、《務農》、《閱武》、《崇文》；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on jichou, the Emperor composed twelve chapters of "Imperial Norms" to bestow on the Crown Prince, titled "The Ruler's Substance," "Establishing Kinship," "Seeking the Worthy," "Examining Officials," "Receiving Remonstrance," "Removing Slander," "Guarding against Fullness," "Honoring Frugality," "Rewards and Punishments," "Devotion to Agriculture," "Review of Arms," and "Honoring Culture";
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on jichou, Emperor Taizong completed twelve chapters of Imperial Norms for the Crown Prince—The Ruler's Substance, Establishing Kin, Seeking Worthies, Examining Officials, Receiving Remonstrance, Removing Slander, Guarding against Excess, Honoring Frugality, Rewards and Punishments, Devotion to Agriculture, Military Review, and Honoring Literature;

sentences.zh: 且曰：「修身治國，備在其中。

translations.literal: He also said: "Cultivating the person and governing the state are all provided for within them.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Everything needed to cultivate yourself and govern the realm is contained in these pages.

sentences.zh: 一旦不諱，更無所言矣。」

translations.literal: Once the tabooed day comes, there will be nothing more to say."
translations.idiomatic: When death comes, I will have nothing left to tell you."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「汝當更求古之哲王以為師，如吾，不足法也。

translations.literal: He also said: "You should further seek the wise kings of antiquity to take as teachers; as for one like Us, it is not enough to take as law.
translations.idiomatic: He went on, "You must find the sage rulers of old and make them your teachers. A man like me is no model worth following.

sentences.zh: 夫取法於上，僅得其中；

translations.literal: When one takes law from what is above, one barely attains the middle;
translations.idiomatic: Aim at the highest standard and you may reach only the middle;

sentences.zh: 取法於中，不免為下。

translations.literal: when one takes law from the middle, one cannot escape being below.
translations.idiomatic: aim at the middle and you will sink to the lowest.

sentences.zh: 吾居位已來，不善多矣，錦繡珠玉不絕於前，宮室台榭屢有興作，犬馬鷹隼無遠不致，行遊四方，供頓煩勞，此皆吾之深過，勿以為是而法之。

translations.literal: Since We took the throne, Our wrongs have been many: brocades and pearls and jade unceasing before Us, palaces and terraces repeatedly raised, dogs and horses and hawks and falcons brought from no distance too far, traveling in all four directions with provisioning and halts vexing and toilsome—all these are Our deep faults; do not take them as right and make them your law.
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the throne my faults have been many—silks and jewels without end, palaces and pavilions raised again and again, hounds and horses and hunting birds fetched from the ends of the earth, journeys in every direction that burdened the people with supplies and camps. These are my gravest errors; do not treat them as examples to follow.

sentences.zh: 顧我弘濟蒼生，其益多；

translations.literal: Yet as for Our broadly succoring the black-haired people, the benefits were many;
translations.idiomatic: Yet in bringing relief to the common people, my benefits were great;

sentences.zh: 肇造區夏，其功大。

translations.literal: in founding and creating the central domains, the achievement was great.
translations.idiomatic: in founding this realm, my achievements were weighty.

sentences.zh: 益多損少，故人不怨；

translations.literal: Benefits many and harms few—therefore the people did not resent;
translations.idiomatic: Benefits outweighed harms, so the people did not resent me;

sentences.zh: 功大過微，故業不墮；

translations.literal: achievement great and faults slight—therefore the enterprise did not fall.
translations.idiomatic: achievements outweighed faults, so the dynasty did not decline;

sentences.zh: 然比之盡美盡善，固多愧矣。

translations.literal: Yet compared with complete beauty and complete goodness, there was indeed much to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: yet compared with perfect virtue, I have much to regret.

sentences.zh: 汝無我之功或而承我之富貴，竭力為善，則國家僅安；

translations.literal: You lack even a portion of Our achievements yet inherit Our wealth and honor—if you exert your strength in doing good, then the state will barely be secure;
translations.idiomatic: You may lack even a fraction of my achievements yet inherit my wealth and rank; if you strive with all your might to do good, the realm may barely endure;

sentences.zh: 驕惰奢縱，則一身不保。

translations.literal: if you are arrogant, lazy, extravagant, and unrestrained, then even your own person will not be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: if you grow arrogant, indolent, extravagant, and unrestrained, not even your own life will be safe.

sentences.zh: 且成遲敗速者，國也；

translations.literal: Moreover, what is achieved slowly and ruined swiftly is the state;
translations.idiomatic: Remember: a state is built slowly but destroyed quickly;

sentences.zh: 失易得難者，位也；

translations.literal: what is lost easily and gained with difficulty is the throne.
translations.idiomatic: a throne is lost easily and won only with difficulty.

sentences.zh: 可不惜哉！

translations.literal: Can you not cherish it!
translations.idiomatic: Will you not cherish it!

sentences.zh: 可不惜哉！」

translations.literal: How can it not be cherished!"
translations.idiomatic: How could one fail to cherish it!"

sentences.zh: 中書令兼右庶子馬周病，上親為調藥，使太子臨問；

translations.literal: Zhongshu Ling and concurrent Right Censor-in-Chief Ma Zhou fell ill; the Emperor personally compounded medicine for him and had the Crown Prince visit to inquire;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhou, Grand Councilor and concurrent Right Censor-in-Chief, fell ill; Emperor Taizong personally prepared his medicine and sent the Crown Prince to visit him;

sentences.zh: 庚寅，薨。

translations.literal: On gengyin, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he died.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，上幸驪山溫湯。

translations.literal: On wuxu, the Emperor traveled in felicity to the hot springs at Mount Li.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Emperor Taizong visited the hot springs at Mount Li.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以中書舍人崔仁師為中書侍郎，參知機務。

translations.literal: On jihai, Zhongshu Sheriff Cui Renshi was made Zhongshu Vice Director, participating in knowing state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Cui Renshi was promoted from Secretariat drafter to Vice Director of the Secretariat with a role in central policy.

sentences.zh: 新羅王金善德卒，以善德妹真德為柱國，封樂浪郡王，遣使冊命。

translations.literal: Silla king Kim Seondeok died; Seondeok's younger sister Jindeok was made Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Prince of Lelang commandery, and envoys were dispatched to invest her.
translations.idiomatic: King Seondeok of Silla died. His sister Queen Jindeok was named Pillar of State, created Prince of Lelang commandery, and envoys were sent to invest her.

sentences.zh: 丙午，詔以右武衛大將軍薛萬徹為青丘道行軍大總管，右衛將軍裴行方副之，將兵三萬餘人及樓船戰艦自萊州泛海以擊高麗。

translations.literal: On bingwu, an edict appointed Right Martial Guard General Xue Wanche as campaign commander of the Qingqiu route, Right Guard General Pei Xingfang as deputy, to lead more than thirty thousand troops and tower-ship warships from Laizhou to sail the sea and strike Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the court named Xue Wanche, general of the Right Martial Guard, commander of the Qingqiu expedition with Pei Xingfang of the Right Guard as his deputy, to lead more than thirty thousand men and tower ships from Laizhou by sea against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌檢校中書令、知尚書門下省事。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji was made acting Zhongshu Ling and charged with knowing the affairs of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji was appointed acting Grand Councilor and put in charge of Secretariat and Chancellery affairs.

sentences.zh: 戊申，上還宮。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Emperor Taizong returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 結骨自古未通中國，聞鐵勒諸部皆服，二月，其俟利發失缽屈阿棧入朝。

translations.literal: Jiegu since antiquity had not communicated with China; hearing that all the Tiele tribes had submitted, in the second month its irkin Shibiequ Aqian entered court.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiegu people had never had contact with China. Learning that the Tiele tribes had all submitted, in the second month their chieftain Shibiequ Aqian came to court.

sentences.zh: 其國人皆長大，赤髮綠睛，有黑髮者以為不祥。

translations.literal: The people of that state were all tall and large, with red hair and green eyes; those with black hair were regarded as inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Its people were tall, with red hair and green eyes; anyone with black hair was considered ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 上宴之於天成殿，謂侍臣曰：「昔渭橋斬三突厥首，自謂功多，今斯人在席，更不以為怪邪！」

translations.literal: The Emperor feasted them in Tiancheng Hall and told his attendants: "In former days at Wei Bridge We beheaded three Türk chiefs and thought Our achievement great—now these men sit at the feast; do you not find it even less strange!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong entertained them in Tiancheng Hall and told his courtiers, "Long ago at Wei Bridge I beheaded three Turk leaders and thought it a great feat—yet these men sit at my table and you are not astonished!"

sentences.zh: 失缽屈阿棧請除一官，「執笏而歸，誠百世之幸。」

translations.literal: Shibiequ Aqian requested that one office be removed for him: "To return holding the court tablet would truly be a fortune for a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: Shibiequ Aqian asked to be given an office: "To return bearing a court tablet would be the blessing of a hundred lifetimes."

sentences.zh: 戊午，以結骨為堅昆都督府，以失缽屈阿棧為右屯衛大將軍、堅昆都督，隸燕然都護。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Jiegu was made the Jiankun Protectorate commandery; Shibiequ Aqian was made Right Tunwei Guard General and Jiankun Protector, subordinate to the Yanran Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Jiegu was organized as the Jiankun Protectorate, Shibiequ Aqian was named general of the Right Tunwei Guard and protector of Jiankun under the Yanran Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 又以阿史德時健俟斤部落置祁連州，隸靈州都督。

translations.literal: Also, from the Ashide Shijian irkin tribe Qilian Prefecture was established, subordinate to the Lingzhou Protector.
translations.idiomatic: The Ashide Shijian tribe was also organized as Qilian Prefecture under the protector of Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時四夷大小君長爭遣使入獻見，道路不絕，每元正朝賀，常數百千人。

translations.literal: At this time the great and small chieftains of the four barbarians vied to send envoys to enter and present tribute; the roads were unceasing, and at each New Year's court congratulations there were commonly several hundred or a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: At this time chieftains great and small from the four quarters competed to send envoys with tribute; the roads never emptied, and hundreds or thousands would attend each New Year's audience.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，上引見諸胡使者，謂侍臣曰：「漢武帝窮兵三十餘年，疲弊中國，所獲無幾；

translations.literal: On xinyou, the Emperor led in audience the various Hu envoys and told his attendants: "Emperor Wu of Han exhausted troops for more than thirty years, wore out China, and gained little;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Emperor Taizong received the foreign envoys and told his courtiers, "Emperor Wu of Han waged war for more than thirty years, exhausted China, and gained little;

sentences.zh: 豈如今日綏之以德，使窮發之地盡為編戶乎！」

translations.literal: how does that compare with today, soothing them with virtue so that lands even of Qiongfa all become registered households!"
translations.idiomatic: how does that compare with soothing them with virtue today until even the farthest lands become registered households of the empire!"

sentences.zh: 上營玉華宮，務令儉約，惟所居殿覆以瓦，餘皆茅茨；

translations.literal: The Emperor built Yuhua Palace, striving to make it frugal and plain; only the hall in which he dwelt was roofed with tiles—the rest were all thatched.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong built Yuhua Palace and insisted on austerity: only the hall he lived in was roofed with tiles, the rest thatched with straw;

sentences.zh: 然備設太子宮、百司，苞山絡野，所費已巨億計。

translations.literal: Yet the Crown Prince's palace and the hundred offices were fully provided; embracing mountains and linking wilds, the expense already ran to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: yet it included a full crown prince's residence and every government office, sprawling across hills and valleys at a cost already reckoned in the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，上行幸玉華宮；

translations.literal: On yihai, the Emperor traveled in felicity to Yuhua Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Emperor Taizong visited Yuhua Palace;

sentences.zh: 己卯，畋於華原。

translations.literal: on jimao, he hunted at Huayuan.
translations.idiomatic: on jimao he hunted at Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎崔仁師坐有伏閣自訴者，仁師不奏，除名，流連州。

translations.literal: Zhongshu Vice Director Cui Renshi sat in guilt because someone had lain prostrate at the palace gate to plead his case and Renshi did not memorialize it; his name was removed and he was banished to Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Cui Renshi was dismissed and exiled to Lianzhou because a petitioner had lain prostrate at the palace gate and Renshi failed to report it.

sentences.zh: 三月，己丑，分瀚海都督俱羅勃部置燭龍州。

translations.literal: In the third month, on jichou, from the tribe of Hanhai Protector Jurubo Zhulong Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jichou, Zhulong Prefecture was carved out of the Jurubo tribe under the Hanhai Protector.

sentences.zh: 甲午，上謂侍臣曰：「朕少長兵間，頗能料敵；

translations.literal: On jiawu, the Emperor told his attendants: "We grew up amid armies and can rather well forecast the enemy;
