translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Emperor Taizong told his courtiers, "I grew up in camp and know how to read an enemy;

sentences.zh: 今昆丘行師，處月、處密二部及龜茲用事者羯獵顛、那利每懷首鼠，必先授首，弩失畢其次也。」

translations.literal: now on the Kunqiu march, the two tribes of Chuyue and Chumi and the Kucha power-holders Jieliedian and Nali each harbor a rat's head and weasel's tail—they will surely offer their heads first; Nushibi will be next."
translations.idiomatic: on this Kunqiu campaign, the Chuyue and Chumi tribes and Kucha's power brokers Jieliedian and Nali are wavering—they will be the first to lose their heads, and Nushibi will follow."

sentences.zh: 庚子，隋蕭後卒。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Sui empress Xiao died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Empress Xiao of Sui died.

sentences.zh: 詔復其位號，謚曰愍；

translations.literal: An edict restored her titles and rank; her posthumous title was Min;
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored her titles and gave her the posthumous name Min;

sentences.zh: 使三品護葬，備鹵簿儀衛，送至江都，與煬帝合葬。

translations.literal: third-rank officials were sent to escort the burial, full regalia and guards of honor were provided, and she was conveyed to Jiangdu to be buried together with Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: third-rank officials escorted the funeral with full imperial regalia to Jiangdu, where she was buried beside Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 充容長城徐惠以上東征高麗，西討龜茲，翠微、玉華，營繕相繼，又服玩頗華靡，上疏諫，其略曰：「以有盡之農功，填無窮之巨浪；

translations.literal: Palace Lady of Fullness Changcheng Xu Hui, because the Emperor was campaigning east against Goguryeo and west against Kucha, with Cuwei and Yuhua and construction following in succession, and also because dress and ornaments were quite lavish and extravagant, submitted a memorial of remonstrance; its gist said: "With finite agricultural labor to fill endless great waves;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Lady Xu Hui of Changcheng, seeing Emperor Taizong's eastern campaign against Goguryeo and western strike at Kucha, the successive building of Cuwei and Yuhua palaces, and his taste for lavish finery, submitted a memorial of remonstrance that began, "To pour finite farm labor into endless seas;

sentences.zh: 圖未獲之他眾，喪已成之我軍。

translations.literal: to scheme for other peoples not yet obtained, and lose an army of Our own already formed.
translations.idiomatic: to chase peoples not yet won while destroying armies already raised.

sentences.zh: 昔秦皇併吞六國，反速危亡之基，晉武奄有三方，翻成覆敗之業；

translations.literal: In former days the First Emperor of Qin swallowed and annexed the six states, yet instead swiftly laid the foundation of peril and ruin; Jin Emperor Wu covered the three regions, yet turned it into an enterprise of overturn and defeat;
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin swallowed six kingdoms yet hastened his own ruin; Emperor Wu of Jin held three realms yet brought on collapse—

sentences.zh: 豈非矜功恃大，棄德輕邦，圖利忘危，肆情縱欲之所致乎！

translations.literal: was it not because they prized achievement and relied on greatness, abandoned virtue and slighted the realm, schemed for profit and forgot peril, and gave free rein to feeling and indulged desire!
translations.idiomatic: was it not because they boasted of conquest, trusted in sheer might, cast aside virtue, scorned their realm, grasped profit and forgot danger, and indulged every appetite!

sentences.zh: 是知地廣非常安之術，人勞乃易亂之源也。」

translations.literal: From this one knows that broad territory is not a technique of extraordinary security, and that when the people are toiled upon that is the source from which disorder comes easily."
translations.idiomatic: This shows that vast territory is no guarantee of lasting peace, and that an overworked people is the seedbed of rebellion."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「雖復茅茨示約，猶興木石之疲，和雇取人，不無煩擾之弊。」

translations.literal: She also said: "Even if thatched huts display frugality, still the weariness of timber and stone is raised; hiring labor and taking men—there is no lack of the harm of vexation and trouble."
translations.idiomatic: She added, "Even building thatched halls to show restraint still exhausts men with timber and stone; hiring laborers still brings harassment in its train."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「珍玩伎巧，乃喪國之斧斤；

translations.literal: She also said: "Rare curios and skilled trickery are the axe and adze that destroy a state;
translations.idiomatic: She also wrote, "Curios and clever crafts are the axe that fells a state;

sentences.zh: 珠玉錦繡，實迷心之鴆毒。」

translations.literal: pearls and jade, brocade and embroidery, are in truth the zhen poison that bewilders the heart."
translations.idiomatic: pearls, jade, silks, and brocades are the poison that clouds the mind."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「作法於儉，猶恐其奢；

translations.literal: She also said: "When one makes law from frugality, one still fears luxury;
translations.idiomatic: She also said, "Set a standard of frugality and you may still fear excess;

sentences.zh: 作法於奢，何以制後！」

translations.literal: when one makes law from luxury, how can one control those who come after!"
translations.idiomatic: set a standard of luxury—how will you restrain those who follow!"

sentences.zh: 上善其言，甚禮重之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved her words and greatly honored and esteemed her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong approved her counsel and treated her with great respect.
